CL

Claude Code

Current · researched 2026-10-11T11:46:24Z

Characteristics

Claude Code is Anthropic's task-oriented coding agent: it reads project files, generates and edits implementation code across files, executes commands, and iterates on results. Its verified strengths include natural-language feature implementation, test generation, refactoring, Git operations, and execution-based error recovery. It is an agentic workflow tool, not merely a source of code snippets. These capabilities describe supported workflows, not guaranteed correctness or performance. Overview

The final merged research distinguishes broad positive capabilities from unresolved ones. Code-editor inline completion and repository-wide meaning-based, relevance-ranked semantic search remain uncertain; prompt autocomplete, grep, and LSP navigation must not be presented as confirmation of those features. Supported local-model inference and full zero-network operation were not found under the completed negative protocols.

Access methods

Access spans a standalone CLI, the VS Code extension with a documented Cursor installation path, a JetBrains plugin, Claude Desktop's Code tab, and browser cloud sessions at claude.ai/code. The Claude iOS and Android apps can start, monitor, and steer remote coding work; code executes in cloud infrastructure or on a connected computer, not on the phone. JetBrains requires a separately installed CLI and retains a Beta label. Desktop includes the engine without a separate CLI; Ubuntu/Debian Desktop support is beta. Overview

The CLI supports macOS, Linux/WSL, and native Windows. Browser onboarding requires GitHub authorization and repository access; eligible Team/Enterprise organizations can use GitHub Enterprise Server. Cloud sessions require Pro, Max, Team, or eligible Enterprise seats, while Console and supported third-party provider access are documented for local CLI/IDE surfaces, not as interchangeable credentials for mobile or cloud sessions. The free Claude chat plan does not include Claude Code.

Exact Pro monthly or annual, Max, and organizational seat prices are not asserted: the registered pricing page's fetched content confirmed usage terms but did not expose paid-plan price cards. Subscription activity across Claude surfaces shares limits; API session cost estimates are not subscription invoices. Usage FAQ

Internal tools and mechanisms

The execution loop combines file reading/searching, file edits, shell commands, tests, and Git with feedback from tool results. Plan mode exposes a proposed implementation plan before editing, and per-tool allow/ask/deny rules provide more granular control than a single autonomy switch. Auto mode removes routine prompts using a model-dependent classifier; it is not equivalent to removing all safeguards. In VS Code Manual mode, side-by-side proposed edits can be accepted or rejected per change on supported versions.

Project CLAUDE.md and auto memory carry context across sessions. Nested/path-scoped instructions, isolated subagent research, and compaction help manage large repositories, but do not establish a repository-size performance guarantee or an embedding index. Instruction scopes are concatenated, with partial, not guaranteed, conflict precedence; managed settings enforcement is a separate mechanism.

Built-in Explore, Plan, and General-purpose agents cover read-only research and broader multi-step work. Custom subagents can define prompts, tools, permissions, hooks, and skills, subject to plugin-specific restrictions. Lifecycle hooks can enforce decisions around actions; skills package repeatable procedures. Native mods can register callable tools without a separate MCP server on supported engine versions. Formatting and linting examples use hooks/project tooling rather than establishing a universal bundled formatter. Subagents

Checkpoint rewind can restore tracked code and conversation together, but shell side effects, most subagent edits, external changes, and skipped linked paths are outside its restoration scope. It complements, rather than replaces, version control.

Workflows and use cases

Documented workflows include implementing a feature across files, exploring an unfamiliar codebase, diagnosing a reported bug, modernizing legacy APIs, generating edge-case tests, and iterating after test failures. Images and mockups can be used to request CSS or HTML structure. Git workflows stage changes, write commits, create branches, and open PRs; local GitHub/GitLab submission requires configured hosting CLIs and credentials. Common workflows

For automation, headless print mode provides non-interactive runs, structured output, and documented exit semantics when credentials and permissions are provisioned. Background agent view can monitor independent local sessions; cloud sessions continue after the client disconnects. Parallel independent tasks are distinct from subagents collaborating on one task. Cloud routines provide scheduled/event-driven work, while Desktop scheduling requires an open app and awake computer.

Managed GitHub Code Review posts inline findings on configured PR events for Team/Enterprise organizations in research preview. It neither approves PRs nor blocks merging. The documented MCP issue-tracker workflow can turn an issue into implementation and a PR, but requires the relevant connector.

Inferred deployment pattern: a controlled team pilot can combine approved plans, narrow permissions, shell sandboxing, headless execution, and customer-operated telemetry. This is a synthesis of verified features, not a vendor promise of safe autonomous operation or a compliance certification.

Integrations

The verified official integration catalog covers Chrome, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI/CD, and Slack, with dedicated documentation; this is a conservative set of confirmed examples, not an exhaustive ecosystem inventory. GitLab CI/CD is beta and maintained by GitLab. Chrome access has plan, login, browser, extension-version, and WSL restrictions. The earlier per-user Slack integration serves Pro/Max channel mentions, while Team/Enterprise use a separate Claude Tag setup path; the two should not be conflated. Platforms and integrations

MCP connects remote HTTP or local stdio servers for tools, databases, and APIs, including customer-authored servers. The documentation points to reviewed Directory connectors and a first-party server-scaffolding plugin, but extraction limitations prevent an exhaustive catalog claim. External content and servers still require trust assessment. MCP reference

Static analysis can feed language-server diagnostics into the agent through a code-intelligence plugin and separately installed server binary; the verified LSP path does not run in cloud sessions. Dependency vulnerability scanning is available through Snyk MCP, which queries Snyk's vulnerability database, rather than a confirmed native Claude CVE scanner. Snyk requires its own setup/authentication and may run ecosystem tools.

Security

Verified controls include per-tool allow/ask/deny permissions, lifecycle decision hooks, local OS-enforced shell sandboxing, network-domain rules, organization SSO/access management, and centrally configured OpenTelemetry export. The sandbox is off by default, available on macOS/Linux/WSL2 rather than native Windows, and limits shell commands and descendants—not every file/web tool, hook, MCP server, or mod. Excluded commands and unsandboxed retries require additional policy decisions. Customer-operated telemetry export is not a vendor-hosted immutable audit archive.

Prompts and outputs travel over the network with TLS 1.2+; Anthropic API infrastructure documents AES-256 disk encryption at rest, with provider-specific alternatives. Local session transcripts are plaintext. Commercial use is not used for generative-model training by default unless the customer opts in; consumer accounts have a model-improvement preference, with thirty-day retention when disabled rather than zero retention. Qualified Enterprise ZDR is separately enabled and excludes several cloud workflows. Feedback and optional survey transcript-sharing have separate retention rules. Data usage

Secret detection/redaction is partial: known-pattern protections are verified in diagnostic, feedback, debug, and shared-transcript paths, not comprehensive filtering of ordinary prompts or generated source. Commercial-contract IP indemnification is confirmed with material exclusions, but a configurable public-code duplication filter is not established. A public DPA applies through Commercial Terms to Team/Enterprise/API use, not automatically to consumer Pro/Max. The DPA links an official subprocessor list, but original-page itemized disclosure could not be verified; that feature remains uncertain.

API workspace geography can constrain inference to US infrastructure on supported models, with separate workspace-storage geography and pricing implications. This does not establish EU first-party residency or a subscription-wide guarantee covering every cloud/telemetry flow. Self-hosted environments host execution on customer runners, not a fully private or offline model service; session content still reaches Anthropic.

Constraints

Availability is surface-, plan-, provider-, model-, and version-dependent. Agent view, cloud routines, and managed Code Review are research previews; self-hosted environments are public beta and disabled by default. Self-hosted runners require Team/Enterprise enablement and customer-managed isolation, egress, and credentials. They retain Anthropic control-plane/session-streaming connectivity and are unavailable for organizations with ZDR or HIPAA configuration. Cloud sessions and managed Code Review also have ZDR/HIPAA restrictions; Code Review is not covered by Anthropic's BAA.

VS Code requires 1.94.0 or later, and verified per-change edit review requires Claude Code 2.1.275+; diffs over 100 changes fall back to whole-file review. Mods require documented engine minimums of 2.1.287 in the terminal and 2.1.286 in Desktop, and are not sandboxed. Local Desktop schedules require Desktop 1.1.5368+ and an awake machine. Auto mode has model/provider eligibility rules and can be disabled by administrators. Not all local configuration, plugin language servers, or credentials transfer into cloud sessions.

Internet access and a supported region are documented setup requirements. Local execution and self-hosted runners do not imply supported local/offline inference. Generated changes, test repair, refactoring, and PR findings need human review and suitable test/build dependencies. Checkpoints cannot reverse arbitrary shell or external side effects, and conflicting custom instructions have no guaranteed scope override.

Subscription limits are shared across surfaces; background work and parallel agents still consume capacity. Exact Pro monthly and annual, Max, Team, and Enterprise prices were not verified from the registered pricing page's paid-plan cards and are intentionally omitted. Connector-directory and marketplace extraction gaps remain relevant to the uncertain semantic-search result; inline editor completion and public itemized subprocessor disclosure also remain uncertain, not absent. The captured release history is limited to the ten most recent official changelog entries checked on October 11, 2026, ending at 2.1.296; an installation on the stable update channel may lag that version.

Use cases

  • Pilot controlled organizational coding automation Inferred

    A team could combine reviewed plans, narrow tool permissions, sandbox boundaries, and customer-operated telemetry export to pilot unattended coding with observable activity. Administrators must configure these controls; telemetry is not a vendor-hosted immutable audit archive and the sandbox does not contain every extension.

    Why inferred: The merged research separately verifies planning approval, per-tool rules, local shell isolation, organizational OpenTelemetry export, and headless execution. Their combination supports this deployment pattern, but no vendor end-to-end compliance certification or guaranteed safe autonomy is inferred.

    Supporting features: plan_visibility_before_executionpermission_autonomy_granularitysandboxed_execution_environmentaudit_loggingheadless_ci_mode

  • Turn a visual mockup into frontend code Documented

    Attach a screenshot or design image and request matching CSS or an HTML component structure. Treat generated UI code as a starting point for review and visual testing.

    • “Generate CSS to match this design mockup”
  • Generate tests and repair failures Documented

    Add scaffolding and edge cases for existing code using the repository's test conventions, then run the generated tests and fix failures. The test framework and executable dependencies must be available.

    • “Claude examines your existing test files to match the style, frameworks, and assertion patterns already in use.”
    • “run the new tests and fix any failures”
  • Implement and verify a multi-file feature Documented

    Describe a feature in natural language, let Claude Code coordinate implementation across files, and verify the change with available project tools. Review the result; vendor-described verification is not a correctness guarantee.

    • “Describe what you want in plain language. Claude Code plans the approach, writes the code across multiple files, and verifies it works.”
  • Implement an issue through MCP and open a PR Documented

    Connect an issue-tracker MCP server so the agent can read requirements directly and implement the requested feature before creating a GitHub PR. This requires the appropriate connectors, repository access, and credentials; it is not a connector-free native Jira capability.

    • “Add the feature described in JIRA issue ENG-4521 and create a PR on GitHub.”
  • Explore an unfamiliar repository Documented

    Ask for a repository overview, architecture patterns, key models, and an explanation of authentication flow. This is documented code exploration, not a claim that repository search uses embeddings or relevance-ranked semantic retrieval.

    • “give me an overview of this codebase”
    • “trace the login process from front-end to database”
  • Schedule repository maintenance Documented

    Use cloud routines for recurring PR reviews, CI failure analysis, or dependency audits when the computer is off; use Desktop scheduling for tasks requiring local files and tools. Cloud routines are in research preview, and local Desktop tasks require an awake computer and open app. Vulnerability-database scanning requires a configured integration such as Snyk rather than an LLM review alone.

    • “Run Claude on a schedule to automate work that repeats: morning PR reviews, overnight CI failure analysis, weekly dependency audits, or syncing docs after PRs merge.”
    • “Tasks that should run even when your computer is off.”
  • Modernize legacy code with regression checks Documented

    Locate deprecated APIs, request a behavior-preserving refactor, and run tests afterward. Work in small increments and verify compatibility instead of assuming the agent formally preserves behavior.

    • “refactor utils.js to use ES2024 features while maintaining the same behavior”
    • “Do refactoring in small, testable increments”

Features

Code Authoring & Editing

  • Uncertain Inline code completion
    No verified official page accessed in this task confirms ambient, as-you-type code-editor ghost text. The IDE pages describe explicitly prompted assistance, diffs, and selection sharing. Interactive-mode autocomplete is in the prompt input and file-path mentions, so it is excluded. The search summary asserted absence but largely cited third-party material and cannot substantiate a feature status. Exhaustive negative coverage was not completed, so absence is not claimed.
  • Has Natural-language-to-code generation
    Claude Code documents generating implementation code from a plain-language feature description, including multiple files and execution-based verification. Concrete workflows also generate test scaffolding and test cases from instructions, beyond short snippets or inline completion.
    plan_or_license
  • Has Multi-file code generation
    The official overview explicitly describes a plain-language feature request leading to planning, writing code across multiple files, and verification in one coordinated workflow.
    plan_or_license
  • Has Automated refactoring
    Official workflows document AI-driven modernization of a file while maintaining behavior, including identifying deprecated APIs, proposing structural changes, applying the refactor, and testing it. This is broader than a single-symbol rename and does not depend on a manual IDE refactor command. The overview confirms that the coding engine can coordinate work across multiple files.
    other
  • Has Diff review and selective apply
    The VS Code extension in Manual mode shows original and proposed content before asking permission to edit. Users can accept or reject individual changes, edit the proposal, and then finish the whole-file review. This satisfies both pre-write review and selective application, rather than merely showing a post-edit diff.
    platform_or_ide product_version other plan_or_license
  • Has Multimodal input (image/screenshot to code)
    The official image workflow documents attaching actual images by drag-and-drop, clipboard paste, or file path, then deriving CSS or HTML from a design mockup. This is code generation from visual input, not merely image description.
    platform_or_ide

Agentic Execution & Runtime

  • Has Autonomous multi-step task execution
    Claude Code decomposes tasks, chooses tools, chains edits and commands, verifies results, and adjusts its approach in an agentic loop. Auto mode and cloud routines provide execution without routine step-by-step confirmation; autonomy is not limited to fixed workflows.
    other other
  • Has Background / long-running task execution
    Agent view dispatches full Claude Code sessions that continue without an attached terminal while the user does other work. It sends completion or failure notifications through the configured terminal channel while agent view is open. Cloud sessions additionally continue after the user's laptop closes.
    release_stage other plan_or_license
  • Has Terminal command execution
    Claude Code directly executes shell commands and receives output to inform subsequent actions. Manual mode asks for shell approval except built-in read-only commands; allow rules, auto mode, and sandbox auto-allow change that confirmation model.
    other other
  • Has Sandboxed / isolated execution environment
    The built-in shell sandbox provides operating-system-enforced file and network isolation for commands and their child processes. Because sandboxing is available locally on supported platforms, it is not restricted to a particular plan or cloud-hosted mode. It is a command sandbox, not isolation of every tool or of the entire application.
    platform_or_ide other other
  • Has Parallel independent task execution
    Vendor documentation explicitly supports dispatching unrelated full sessions concurrently from one agent-view interface, and independently starting simultaneous cloud tasks. This is independent task concurrency, not delegation of one task to subagents.
    release_stage other plan_or_license
  • Has Self-healing error recovery
    The documented agentic loop runs tests, reads failure output, edits relevant files, and runs tests again within the same task. Bug fixes repeat context/action/verification phases and course-correct without requiring a fresh prompt for each failure. This documents iterative recovery, not a guaranteed always-green result.
    other
  • Has Agent session checkpoint & rollback
    The /rewind menu restores tracked code changes across the session and its conversation to a selected earlier prompt in one operation. This is session-wide rollback, not per-file or per-hunk review. It does not restore every possible side effect: shell modifications and most subagent edits are excluded.
    other other
  • Has Scheduled / recurring task execution
    Native routines save a prompt and environment with recurring or one-time future triggers and execute autonomously in the cloud, without an active user session. Users can create them in the web or Desktop interface or with /schedule in the CLI. Desktop also supports native local scheduled sessions; no third-party cron wrapper is necessary.
    release_stage plan_or_license platform_or_ide product_version

Agent Customization & Orchestration

  • Has Multi-agent / sub-agent orchestration
    Claude Code documents delegating tasks to specialized subagents that execute independently in separate context windows and return results to the main agent. The official overview explicitly describes simultaneous agents with a lead coordinating assignments and merging results. This is supported orchestration within a session, not merely users manually opening independent sessions; no experimental team feature is needed to establish the status.
    other other
  • Has User-defined sub-agent roles
    Users can author Markdown subagent definitions with YAML frontmatter or supply --agents JSON. The Markdown body supplies the system prompt, tools/disallowedTools independently scope access, and permissionMode and mcpServers provide additional per-agent configuration. Project and user definitions are documented supported mechanisms.
    other other
  • Has Custom tool / function-calling API
    The documented native mods API exposes $.tool.register with a name, description, and input JSON Schema, and a JavaScript tool.call handler implements the callable tool in Claude Code's process. Although the exposed tool name uses the mcp__ prefix and supports MCP tool deferral, this mechanism does not require registering or running an MCP server. It therefore meets the non-MCP registration criterion rather than relying on the excluded MCP-only integration or SDK in-process MCP server pattern.
    integration_required product_version platform_or_ide other
  • Has Agent lifecycle hooks
    The official hooks reference documents user-defined command handlers around tool execution, including PreToolUse and PostToolUse. A worked example reads tool input and returns permissionDecision deny to block the action. This is an active lifecycle extension mechanism, not merely a passive notification webhook.
    other platform_or_ide
  • Has Permission / autonomy-level granularity
    Allow, ask, and deny rules can be configured independently by tool and by command/path/domain patterns. File edits can be auto-accepted while other Bash commands still require approval, and explicit ask rules can preserve confirmations even under auto mode. This exceeds a single global autonomy toggle.
    other other model
  • Has Plan visibility before execution
    Plan mode researches and writes a proposed plan before source edits are allowed. The documented approval dialog presents choices to approve with auto mode or manual edit approval, or stay in planning; accepting exits plan mode and starts editing. Users can also edit the proposed plan before proceeding. Research tool calls during planning are distinguished from the subsequent autonomous implementation.
    other platform_or_ide

Context & Code Quality

  • Uncertain Codebase-wide semantic search
    Official workflows document natural-language requests to find code, but do not establish repository-wide meaning-based retrieval ranked by relevance. Current large-codebase and code-intelligence documentation describes grep/file reads and LSP symbol navigation, neither of which alone qualifies. Scoped searches did not establish an embedding or other semantic retrieval integration. The connector directory did not expose its catalog and only part of the large official marketplace catalog was accessed, so an integration may remain undiscovered. The negative protocol is incomplete; not_found would be unjustified.
  • Has Large-repository / long-context handling
    Claude Code documents codebase-specific context management: on-demand nested project instructions, path-scoped rules, excluding irrelevant instructions and generated files, precise symbol navigation, and isolated subagent exploration that returns summaries. For long sessions it automatically compacts conversation history and supports custom compaction instructions. These are mechanisms for repository and task context, not merely a general model context-window size; they do not guarantee performance at a particular repository size.
    other integration_required
  • Has Persistent project memory / custom instructions
    Project CLAUDE.md files persist coding standards and project context in version control and are read automatically at the start of each session. Auto memory additionally saves learned preferences and project knowledge across conversations. These mechanisms are not limited to one session or manual repeated prompting.
    other
  • Has Automated test generation
    The official test workflow explicitly generates scaffolding and edge-case tests for specified existing code, examines existing tests to follow the project's framework and assertion conventions, and runs and fixes the generated tests. No small fixed framework or language set is stated in this workflow.
  • Has Automated code review / PR review
    Claude Code documents a dedicated managed GitHub PR review workflow that automatically analyzes changes and posts inline findings. This satisfies the hosting-integrated criterion rather than merely local diff review. Other plans can use a dedicated local /code-review command, and CI alternatives are documented separately.
    plan_or_license release_stage integration_required other
  • Has Static analysis / linting integration
    Code-intelligence plugins connect a language server directly to Claude Code and feed its errors and warnings to Claude after edits. The diagnostics help Claude identify and fix type, syntax, and import errors, so this is assistant-connected static analysis rather than merely the editor's independent lint display. The documented Snyk MCP integration also exposes SAST findings.
    integration_required platform_or_ide integration_required
  • Has Dependency vulnerability scanning (SCA)
    Dependency scanning is available through the documented Snyk MCP integration, not asserted as a built-in Claude scanner. Anthropic's connector catalog explicitly lists SCA and snyk_sca_scan; Snyk's own Claude Code guide confirms that this tool inspects dependency manifests and queries the Snyk vulnerability database. This directly satisfies the integration-based has criterion. LLM security review alone was not used to substantiate CVE/database matching.
    integration_required other
  • Partial Layered instruction precedence (personal/repository/organization)
    Managed organization, personal user, shared project, and local project instruction scopes load automatically in documented order. However, the documentation explicitly says instructions are concatenated rather than overridden and that conflicting user and project rules may follow either one. Thus this is layered loading without a defined conflict-precedence hierarchy, matching partial rather than has. Enforced settings precedence is distinct and was not substituted for custom-instruction precedence.
    other

    The official overview documents direct Git operation: staging changes, writing commit messages, creating branches, and opening pull requests. This is execution within Claude Code, not merely suggested commands for the user.

A separate official JetBrains plugin additionally supports IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, Android Studio, WebStorm, PhpStorm, and GoLand, but its settings retain a Beta label; that qualification is recorded rather than treating all JetBrains support as unqualified stable support.

These are cloud execution sessions, not merely billing/account pages or browser remote control of an installed local CLI. Cloud sessions continue after the client disconnects.

    Claude Code supports the open MCP protocol for external tools, databases, and APIs, with documented server configuration and instructions for building custom servers. Extensibility is not restricted to a curated vendor catalog.

Additional facts

Built-in tools

  • Bundled tooling:

    Claude Desktop includes the Claude Code engine and does not require a separate CLI installation. Native CLI installations update automatically; Homebrew and WinGet installations require explicit upgrades. Homebrew offers stable and latest casks, so an installed version may intentionally lag the newest changelog. Desktop is available for macOS and Windows, with Ubuntu/Debian support described as beta.

    • “The app includes Claude Code, so you don't need to install the CLI separately.”
    • “Native installations automatically update in the background to keep you on the latest version.”
    • “Homebrew installations do not auto-update.”
    • “On Ubuntu or Debian, where the app is in beta, install it with apt by following the [Linux install instructions](/docs/en/desktop-linux)”
  • Named sub-agents:

    Built-in roles include Explore for read-only code discovery, Plan for read-only planning research, and General-purpose for exploration and modification. Additional helpers include statusline-setup and claude-code-guide. These are built-in roles, distinct from illustrative custom agents such as code-improver. Explore and Plan omit CLAUDE.md and the git status snapshot; model selection and overrides depend on the role and provider.

    • “A fast, read-only agent optimized for searching and analyzing codebases.”
    • “A capable agent for complex, multi-step tasks that require both exploration and action.”
    • “Explore and Plan skip your CLAUDE.md files and the git status snapshot to keep research fast and inexpensive.”
  • Bundled tooling:

    Skills package repeatable workflows for team reuse, while hooks can invoke formatting after edits or linting before commits. These documented extension patterns do not establish that Claude Code bundles a universal formatter or linter; use project tooling or configured language-server integrations.

    • “Create [skills](/docs/en/skills) to package repeatable workflows your team can share, like `/review-pr` or `/deploy-staging`.”
    • “[Hooks](/docs/en/hooks) let you run shell commands before or after Claude Code actions, like auto-formatting after every file edit or running lint before a commit.”

Pricing & licensing

  • Pricing note:

    Subscription activity across Claude web, desktop, mobile, and Claude Code draws from a shared usage pool. Limits depend on conversation complexity, model, and features rather than a fixed message count. The pricing FAQ describes rolling five-hour session windows and additional weekly limits for paid plans; paid users may enable usage credits to continue at standard API rates. Parallel sessions and subagents can consume this shared capacity faster.

    • “Your activity across Claude on web, desktop, mobile, and Claude Code all draws from the same pool.”
    • “Every plan has [usage limits](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9797557-usage-limit-best-practices) that reset on a rolling five-hour session window, and paid plans add weekly limits on top.”
    • “It also sends its own requests, which count toward the same [usage limits](/docs/en/costs#plan-usage-breakdown) as your main conversation.”
  • Pricing note:

    The session dollar figure is calculated locally from token counts at list price or configured organizational rates; it is an estimate, not authoritative billing. For Pro and Max, included subscription usage means that figure is not itself a bill. API customers should use the Console Usage page for authoritative billing and pilot their own workload rather than treating vendor average spend as a promised price.

    • “The figure is an estimate, so for authoritative billing see the Usage page in the [Claude Console](https://platform.claude.com/usage).”
    • “Claude Max and Pro subscribers have usage included in their subscription, so the session cost figure isn't relevant for billing purposes.”

Security & data handling

  • Data usage:

    Feedback submissions through /feedback, /bug, or /share have a separate five-year retention policy. The optional session-quality transcript-sharing follow-up is distinct: selecting Yes shares source and conversation content as-is except known API-key/token patterns, with retention up to six months and no model-training use. Survey ratings alone do not collect transcripts. These paths must not be collapsed into the ordinary training opt-out or thirty-day retention setting.

    • “Transcripts shared via `/feedback`, or via `/bug` and `/share`, which report through the same path, are retained for 5 years.”
    • “Source code, file contents, and other conversation content are uploaded as-is.”
    • “Shared transcripts are retained for up to 6 months.”
    • “Your responses to this survey, including session transcripts submitted after the rating prompt, do not impact your data training preferences and cannot be used to train our AI models.”

Extensibility & MCP ecosystem

  • Extensibility via MCP:

    The MCP reference directs users to reviewed Directory connectors and also supports custom servers, including a first-party mcp-server-dev plugin for scaffolding remote HTTP or local stdio servers. Directory membership is not a security guarantee: server trust and authentication still require evaluation. No exhaustive connector count is asserted.

    • “Browse reviewed connectors in the [Anthropic Directory](https://claude.ai/directory).”
    • “Claude asks about your use case and scaffolds a remote HTTP or local stdio server.”
    • “Verify you trust each server before connecting it.”

CU

Cursor

Current · researched 2026-10-11T12:07:41Z

Characteristics

Cursor combines an AI-enabled editor with agents that search project files, generate and refactor code across multiple files, run terminal commands, generate tests, and iterate on feedback. Tab supplies inline suggestions while typing; Agent handles larger plain-language tasks. Image-based UI implementation is documented with a vision-capable model. These capabilities are established in the merged feature results, not promises of error-free or behavior-preserving output.

The product has several distinct execution surfaces: local editor/CLI work, managed Cloud Agents, and self-hosted tool workers connected to Cursor's cloud agent loop. Parallel independent agents are different from coordinated subagents: the former handle separate tasks, while the latter return delegated results to a parent conversation. Long-session mechanisms include summarized context and isolated exploration. The semantic-search feature remains uncertain because current exact-match/regex documentation and older embedding-based research claims have not been reconciled.

Plan Mode provides a reviewable implementation plan before code-writing when explicitly selected. It is not a universal pre-apply gate: ordinary Agent workspace edits save immediately, so later diff review must not be described as approval before disk writes.

Access methods

The native Cursor editor installs on macOS, Windows, and Linux and requires a Cursor account. The standalone CLI supports terminal-based interactive work and non-interactive print automation, with documented installation routes for macOS, Linux, WSL, and native Windows. CI use requires authentication and Internet access; JSON and stream-json output are available, but failures may end without a well-formed final JSON result.

Cursor Web starts and manages Cloud Agents without a locally installed editor. Paid plans are required for Cloud Agent runs, which incur model-based usage charges. Existing-repository work requires an administrator-connected source-control provider and the user's read-write repository access. A documented start-from-scratch route is an alternative, subject to paid-plan and Origin setup or administrator settings, not a waiver of existing-repository permissions.

The native iPhone/iPad app directs agents, streams progress, accepts follow-ups, and supports PR review rather than providing a full editor, terminal, or file browser. The merged research records iOS/iPadOS 26.0+, paid-plan requirements for starting runs, an English-only interface, and availability excluding mainland China. Native Android is planned; browser/PWA access is distinct. The October 6 changelog also documents remote control of local agents, which requires the computer to remain powered on and online and Enterprise administrator enablement.

Cursor's agent can also run in supported JetBrains IDEs through ACP, with AI Assistant enabled in version 2025.1+ and a paid Cursor plan. This establishes agent access in those IDEs, not parity with every native-editor feature such as Tab.

Internal tools and mechanisms

Agent's verified mechanisms include file search, coordinated file editing, terminal execution, linter feedback, checkpoints, and delegated subagents. Explore and Browser are the two documented built-in subagent roles; custom role files can specify prompts, models, and read-only restrictions. Subagents have independent context windows but share the parent's checkout by default, so concurrent writes can conflict. Requested isolation can use separate worktrees or cloud environments; nesting, Task access, policy, and model billing constraints still apply.

Project .mdc rules and scoped AGENTS.md instructions persist repository guidance. The documented instruction hierarchy merges applicable Team, Project, and User rules, with earlier sources taking precedence in conflicts. These rules are scoped Agent guidance, not model memory or a guarantee that every AI feature receives the same instructions. Tab and Bugbot have different scope; Bugbot uses separate repository instructions.

Lifecycle hooks can observe, block, or modify actions, with cloud-specific event and configuration limitations. Explicit blocking and invalid permission outputs differ from other hook failures that may proceed by default. MCP enables external tools and custom servers. The SDK's customTools path is explicitly MCP-backed, so this profile does not assert an independent native function-registration interface.

Agent checkpoints restore modified files across a session, but do not roll back conversation history, external command effects, or the whole environment. Linter feedback integration is documented for JavaScript/TypeScript with installed linter extensions; it is not evidence of a bundled universal formatter or analyzer.

Workflows and use cases

Vendor-documented workflows include planning a feature before implementation, test-driven development, generating characterization tests before refactoring, turning mockups into UI, scheduled codebase summaries, event-driven bug triage, and continuous PR review with Bugbot. Verification should include suitable tests, type checking, linting, and visual checks rather than accepting generated code solely because an agent reports completion.

Cloud Agents can work in the background on branches and create PRs, while the Agents Window manages many independent tasks. Automatic fixes of CI failures in agent-created PRs are documented for Teams and GitHub Actions, with skip conditions and a ten-follow-up cap; this is not unrestricted automatic repair of every CI system. Long-running agents also have team controls and are not available for multi-repo environments in the merged research.

The use-case records distinguish documented flows from inferred combinations. Parallel maintenance with human merge review, a narrowly scoped headless CI maintenance gate, and team-standardized agent work are inferred from established features, not vendor guarantees. Automated review also needs a deliberate merge policy: Bugbot findings default to a neutral check, so requiring the check alone does not block merges on unresolved findings.

Integrations

Official documentation establishes integrations with GitHub, Slack, Linear, and Notion, and names other source-control providers and JetBrains. This is a confirmed set, not an exhaustive marketplace count. GitHub app installation and organization administration govern repository and PR permissions. Slack and Linear require connected workspaces and Cloud Agent setup. Notion's integration is beta, requires a Notion Business or Enterprise plan, and has additional connection/API-key setup; Cloud Agent usage is still billed.

MCP provides an open extension route with custom servers, local or remote transports, and optional OAuth for remote servers. Enterprise administrators can restrict allowed servers and tools. External integration credentials, permissions, provider policies, and model-boundary exposure must be evaluated separately from Cursor's own controls.

Source-control support varies by capability. Bugbot review, automatic CI fixes, Automation triggers, and multi-repo/long-running execution should not be assumed to have identical provider coverage. The merged research retains public-beta and Data Center limitations for some review integrations. Marketplace dependency-security descriptions do not yet establish the precise vulnerability-database matching criterion.

Security

The merged research confirms Privacy Mode, encryption in transit and at rest, organizational SSO and roles, local sandbox controls, and isolated Cloud Agent VMs. Privacy Mode is an actionable training opt-out, including individual/free users, with team enforcement available. It is not blanket zero retention: abuse investigations, explicitly enabled non-ZDR models, customer-supplied provider keys, and temporary Cloud Agent storage have scoped exceptions. The separate Grok Bot surface must not inherit editor privacy guarantees by assumption.

Terminal commands require local approval by default, but configured Run Modes can reduce approval or run everything. Desktop allowlists and classifier guidance are best-effort convenience, not a security boundary. Local sandboxing is conditional on supported macOS/Linux versions and mode; Run Everything is not sandboxed, and approved escalation can leave sandbox restrictions. Egress policies verified for local sandboxed terminal commands must not be generalized to every tool or Cloud Agent surface.

Configured Cloud Agent Runtime Secrets are redacted from model-visible results and related records. This is partial secret protection, not established discovery of arbitrary credentials in repository files or prompts. Ordinary environment variables remain visible to the agent, and Runtime Secret values remain accessible through the environment terminal.

Teams and Enterprise have SSO and roles; SCIM, per-event audit logs, and programmatic analytics have Enterprise restrictions. Audit logs do not capture every prompt, generated artifact, failed sign-in, or automation run. US-only residency is Enterprise, enabled per team, and limited to eligible models and in-scope features; external integrations, BYOK/custom gateways, and other documented exceptions remain. EU + Iceland availability is inference-only on request, not an equivalent full storage-and-processing commitment.

Public DPA coverage applies to Teams/Enterprise business contracts, not individual plans. The MSA's suggestion IP indemnity is partial under the combined criterion because a built-in public-code duplication-blocking filter was not verified. The itemized subprocessor list remains uncertain after an access denial in the merged research; no vendor list is reconstructed from memory.

Constraints

Deployment and connectivity

Full offline AI operation and a customer-hosted deployment of the whole Cursor service were not found under the completed protocols in the merged feature results. Self-Hosted Machines move tool execution to customer machines while Cursor retains inference, planning, and the agent loop. Selected file contents, outputs, diffs, screenshots, MCP results, and metadata still leave the worker, and outbound HTTPS is required. BYOK also routes through Cursor's backend. Supported local/self-hosted inference remains uncertain despite documentation mentioning a compatible base-URL override.

Plans, models, and platforms

The checked pricing page displays Pro at US$20/month and Teams Standard at US$40/user/month, with custom Enterprise pricing and a limited free Hobby tier; taxes and model usage are separate considerations. Pro/Pro Plus/Ultra have distinct Cursor Models and Other Models pools, while the India-focused Start plan does not include Other Models. Cloud Agent and Automation usage is metered. Model eligibility, administrative restrictions, vision support, context size, and subagent token consumption can change which workflows are available or economical. Desktop, CLI, mobile, browser, and ACP integration capabilities are not interchangeable.

Local sandboxing requires the documented macOS or supported Linux environment; no Windows sandbox parity is asserted. Paid Cloud Agent VMs, self-hosted workers, local Run Modes, and enterprise egress controls have different boundaries. Long-running and multi-repo limitations, repository permissions, and provider-specific review/CI support should be checked before deployment.

Partial and unresolved criteria

Audit logging and DPA availability are partial because of plan/contract restrictions. Runtime Secret redaction is partial because it protects configured values rather than arbitrary secrets. IP protection is partial because MSA indemnification is established but a built-in duplication filter is not. Semantic retrieval, pre-disk-write granular diff approval, MCP-independent custom function registration, supported local/self-hosted inference, database-backed dependency vulnerability scanning, and inspection of the subprocessor list remain uncertain. None is silently promoted to supported or unsupported by this synthesis.

Release and pricing coverage

Release history captures five dated announcements newer than July 10, 2026 from the already-registered official changelog root. Dates were checked in the original HTML, not inferred from slugs, relative wording, or search summaries. The root links to older pagination that is not in the final source registry; releases requiring those pages are omitted and the since-date interval is explicitly incomplete. The pricing extraction initially omitted tier cards, so selected monthly prices were recovered from the original HTML. No exact annual discounts, complete paid-tier allowance table, or numeric free quota is supplied without verified coverage.

Use cases

  • Run bounded repository maintenance from CI Inferred

    Invoke the headless CLI for a narrowly scoped repository task, collect structured output, and use process exit status plus independent checks to decide whether a resulting patch is acceptable. Provide authentication, Internet access, and restrictive permissions; applying edits requires the documented force option. Do not interpret JSON output as assurance of code correctness.

    Why inferred: The merged results confirm non-interactive print mode, JSON/stream-json output, failure exit semantics, CI integration, and independent allow/deny policies. The proposed bounded maintenance gate is inferred from those mechanisms.

    Supporting features: standalone_cliheadless_ci_modepermission_autonomy_granularityterminal_command_execution

  • Generate characterization tests before refactoring Documented

    Generate tests for existing or unfamiliar code using the repository's frameworks and conventions, then run them after refactoring steps to detect regressions. Automatic run-and-fix iteration requires an appropriate Auto-run configuration. Passing generated tests is useful feedback, not proof of complete behavioral equivalence.

    • “Before refactoring, generate tests that lock in current behavior.”
    • “Run these tests after each refactoring step to catch regressions immediately.”
  • Review pull requests continuously with Bugbot Documented

    Connect a supported source-control provider, enable Bugbot on repositories, and receive review comments on updates or request a manual review where supported. Individual settings limit review to the user's own PRs; enabled team repositories can cover all contributors. Check-status configuration must be considered separately from review generation.

    • “Bugbot analyzes PR diffs and leaves comments with explanations and fix suggestions. It runs automatically on each PR update or manually when triggered.”
    • “Bugbot runs for all contributors to enabled repositories, regardless of team membership.”
  • Implement UI from a mockup and iterate on visual feedback Documented

    Paste a screenshot, wireframe, or Figma export into a prompt, ask Agent to implement the component, and use visual feedback to refine it. Direct image input requires a vision-capable model; a Figma MCP connection is optional for richer design data rather than a prerequisite for pasted images.

    • “**Mockups**: Paste a wireframe or Figma export and ask the agent to build the component”
    • “**Iteration**: Take a screenshot of the current result and describe what needs to change”
  • Delegate independent maintenance tasks while retaining merge review Inferred

    Run separate Cloud Agents for independent maintenance changes, inspect their branches and PRs, and merge only after tests and human review. Use separate task scopes to reduce edit contention. Paid-plan eligibility, repository permissions, model costs, and team controls still apply.

    Why inferred: The validated features establish independently running Cloud Agents, parallel task management, branch-based work, and direct PR creation. Combining these into a maintenance queue is a workflow inference, not a new vendor guarantee.

    Supporting features: parallel_independent_task_executionbackground_long_running_tasksgit_native_workflowpull_request_creation

  • Plan and implement a test-driven feature Documented

    Use Plan Mode to research the codebase and edit a stepwise implementation plan, then write and commit tests before requesting code that passes them without changing the tests. Review and verify the result before committing. The vendor documents this workflow; it does not guarantee generated code is correct.

    • “With Cursor's [Plan Mode](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/plan-mode.md), the agent will research your codebase, ask you clarifying questions, and produce a step-by-step plan you can edit and modify.”
    • “Tell it to make all tests pass without modifying the tests.”
  • Schedule codebase digests or trigger event-driven triage Documented

    Configure an Automation with a recurring schedule or supported source-control, Slack, Linear, or webhook event, a prompt, and selected tools. Vendor examples include scheduled codebase summaries and Slack bug triage. Code-changing automations need repository selection; Cloud Agent usage is billed and scheduled execution may be delayed.

    • “Cursor Automations run [cloud agents](https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent.md) in the background, either on a schedule or in response to events from GitHub, GitLab, Slack, webhooks, Linear, and more.”
    • “Scheduled triggers may run with a delay but will not start before the indicated time.”
  • Standardize agent work across a team Inferred

    Combine enforced team guidance, version-controlled project rules, lifecycle checks, and appropriate administrator controls to make repository work more consistent. Test the policies and review outcomes; not all hook failures block actions, and instruction precedence is not a substitute for an execution security boundary.

    Why inferred: The validated hierarchy, persistent rule files, hooks, and organizational access controls support this combined workflow. It remains an inference, with Teams/Enterprise and Enterprise-only distribution constraints retained rather than assuming all controls exist on every plan.

    Supporting features: layered_instruction_precedencepersistent_project_memoryagent_lifecycle_hooksenterprise_sso_access_control

Features

Code Authoring & Editing

  • Has Inline code completion
    Cursor Tab generates grayed-out inline suggestions while typing, without an explicit chat request, and can modify multiple lines. The native Cursor editor workflow is confirmed for macOS, Windows, and Linux. The checked documentation does not enumerate an exhaustive supported-language matrix; no language restriction or support in every external IDE is inferred.
    platform_or_ide other
  • Has Natural-language-to-code generation
    Agent accepts plain-language requests and builds features from scratch, selecting and modifying relevant files. The official feature-development guide documents generating a new function from test-defined requirements and implementing UI components, API routes, and tests in a coordinated plan. Granularity extends from functions/components to multi-file features, rather than only short snippets or inline completion. Runnable correctness still requires verification; documentation does not promise error-free code.
    platform_or_ide plan_or_license other
  • Has Multi-file code generation
    Agent accepts a plain-language task, determines relevant files, and edits multiple files within that task. Official inline-edit help explicitly directs multi-file work to Agent. The known product page also demonstrates coordinated implementation and fixes in several Python modules, so this is not repeated manual single-file invocation.
    other plan_or_license
  • Has Automated refactoring
    Cursor documents plain-language-driven refactoring through Agent, which locates relevant files and edits multiple files. The prompting reference explicitly describes multi-file refactoring, going beyond single-symbol rename or manual IDE commands. This establishes the capability, not a guarantee of behavioral equivalence; tests and human review remain necessary.
    model other
  • Uncertain Diff review and selective apply
    A reviewable diff and rejection workflow are documented, but they do not establish the assigned pre-disk-write criterion: current Agent security documentation explicitly states that changes save immediately to disk, and the help page describes reviewing already-applied edits. Inline edit documentation also says Cursor applies the edit in place without documenting a pre-save, per-hunk gate. The search returned community discussions and summary claims about granular controls, which were not treated as official evidence. Research did not establish whether a separate current workflow satisfies the strict definition, so neither has nor the whole-file-only partial criterion is justified. This is not a not_found result because coverage of alternative pre-apply workflows remains incomplete.
    other
  • Has Multimodal input (image/screenshot to code)
    Current official prompting documentation supports image attachments by drag-and-drop or clipboard, including screenshots, for design implementation. The first-party Developing features guide explicitly instructs users to paste a wireframe or Figma export and ask Agent to build the component. This is image-derived code generation, not merely image description. A Figma MCP connection is optional for pulling richer design data, not required for direct screenshot input. The attempted legacy image URL failed, but accessible current official pages directly establish the capability.
    model

Agentic Execution & Runtime

  • Has Autonomous multi-step task execution
    Agent independently completes complex coding tasks through repeated search, editing and terminal tool calls. Cloud Agents auto-run terminal commands to iterate on tests without step-by-step approval; local Run Modes also support reduced or no per-call confirmation. The capability is not limited to a fixed predefined workflow.
    other plan_or_license
  • Has Background / long-running task execution
    Cloud Agents run independently of the user's connected local machine, and the Agents Window supports handing work to the cloud to keep working on its own. Completion notifications are explicitly documented for Slack. Extended-duration agents are separately subject to team controls.
    plan_or_license integration_required other
  • Has Terminal command execution
    Agent directly executes shell commands and monitors their output. Local execution uses default manual approval or configured Run Modes; cloud execution auto-runs commands to support autonomous test iteration.
    other
  • Has Sandboxed / isolated execution environment
    Cursor documents both isolated cloud VMs and restricted local shell sandboxes. Sandboxing is therefore not confined to a paid cloud mode alone. Local isolation is conditional on platform support and Run Mode; it is not a claim that every command always runs isolated.
    platform_or_ide other plan_or_license
  • Has Parallel independent task execution
    The Cloud Agents documentation explicitly supports running arbitrarily many agents in parallel. The Agents Window manages agents across all projects in one workspace. This evidence concerns independent agent instances, not a coordinator delegating parts of one task to subagents.
    plan_or_license integration_required product_version
  • Has Self-healing error recovery
    Cloud Agents automatically attempt to fix CI failures in their own PRs without a new user prompt, with repeated CI-failure follow-ups capped at ten. The security documentation explicitly describes iterating on tests without per-step approvals. CI subscriptions can also wake the same conversation when checks finish.
    plan_or_license integration_required other
  • Has Agent session checkpoint & rollback
    An Agent checkpoint captures all modified files and a single restore reverts all files to that checkpoint, rather than requiring file-by-file or hunk-by-hunk undo. This is session-wide code rollback, not a rollback of conversation history, command side effects, or the whole operating environment.
    other
  • Has Scheduled / recurring task execution
    Native Cursor Automations let users activate a prompt with recurring preset or cron triggers, running Cloud Agents without an interactive start at the scheduled moment. Cloud Agent timer subscriptions additionally document one-off delayed and recurring triggers. This is native scheduling, not merely an external CI cron invoking a CLI.
    other plan_or_license other

Agent Customization & Orchestration

  • Has Multi-agent / sub-agent orchestration
    The parent agent delegates to isolated-context specialist subagents and collects their results. Documentation covers simultaneous Task calls, sequential orchestrator handoffs, and background execution; this is coordinated work rather than manually running independent chats.
    other other model
  • Has User-defined sub-agent roles
    Users can author named Markdown/YAML subagent definitions with their own prompt, description, model, and independently restricted write permissions via readonly. The documented read-only scope prohibits edits and state-changing shell commands, meeting the tool-scope requirement, although arbitrary per-role tool allowlists and separate MCP attachments are not documented in this file format. These are user-authored roles, not only the built-in Explore and Browser agents.

However, the original documentation explicitly says those functions are registered as an MCP server and called through the MCP path; disallowing mcp also removes them. The assigned definition requires a native mechanism independent of MCP, so this implementation cannot safely be marked has or partial under the supplied criteria. No separate non-MCP registration mechanism was confirmed. A complete negative protocol across all relevant source classes was not performed, so this is uncertain rather than not_found.

  • Has Agent lifecycle hooks
    Documented project/user hooks.json configuration launches custom scripts before and after agent lifecycle stages, including generic tool use, shell execution, reads, edits, and subagent spawning. Hooks can block or modify actions, not merely notify an external service.
    platform_or_ide plan_or_license other
  • Has Permission / autonomy-level granularity
    Desktop permissions independently configure terminal and MCP automatic approval through separate allowlists, rather than only a global run switch. CLI permission tokens additionally control shell, reads, writes, web fetch, and MCP with independent allow/deny entries.
    platform_or_ide other other
  • Has Plan visibility before execution
    Plan Mode creates an implementation plan before code-writing, lets the user review and edit it, and waits for the user to click to build. Preparatory codebase research and clarifying questions occur before plan approval, but implementation is gated by that explicit transition.

Context & Code Quality

  • Uncertain Codebase-wide semantic search
    Original official research pages explicitly describe natural-language semantic retrieval using a trained embedding model and codebase indexing. However, the current Search documentation describes exact-match/regex Instant Grep and states that Cursor does not store codebase embeddings for search. Its Explore subagent is a context-management mechanism, not evidence of relevance-ranked semantic retrieval. Scope and current-capability policy favor the documentation over research articles, but the fetched pages do not establish whether semantic retrieval survives in another supported product surface or whether the research claims are historical. A broader changelog search did not provide original verified deprecation/version evidence. Consequently neither a current has/partial claim nor a completed negative finding is warranted.
  • Has Large-repository / long-context handling
    Current documentation provides both repository-scale handling and long-session handling without relying solely on a model's nominal context-window size: Instant Grep is optimized for large codebases; Explore subagents search in their own context windows and return summarized relevant findings; Cursor compresses older conversation content when the main context approaches capacity. These are documented mechanisms, not an independent guarantee of output quality or a benchmark claim.
    other platform_or_ide model
  • Has Persistent project memory / custom instructions
    Version-controlled .cursor/rules/*.mdc files persist project-specific conventions and guidance. Always Apply rules are automatically included in every chat session; path-pattern and relevance-based rules provide additional automatic scope selection. Nested AGENTS.md instructions are also automatically applied when working in the corresponding directory. This is persistent project guidance, not a claim that the underlying model retains memory between completions.
    other other other other
  • Has Automated test generation
    Cursor explicitly documents generating unit tests for an existing named service file, matching the repository's test patterns, and generating integration and end-to-end tests across multiple frameworks. This is documented test generation, rather than an incidental example of general code generation.

  • Has Automated code review / PR review
    Bugbot is a dedicated hosting-platform PR review workflow, not an ad hoc chat request. It analyzes PR diffs, posts explanations and suggested fixes, and automatically reruns on PR updates. The accepted GitHub integration source independently documents connecting repositories for Bugbot.

  • Has Static analysis / linting integration
    Official JS/TS documentation explicitly states that Cursor integrates with linter extensions and that Agent reads their output after making changes and attempts to repair lint errors. Findings therefore feed the AI's next edits rather than being displayed only by the editor.

Cursor's first-party marketplace exposes Snyk and Sonatype-related descriptions, but the fetched content did not verify a project-dependency scan against a named vulnerability database with surfaced results. Security & Governance

  • Has Enterprise SSO / access control
    Cursor supports SAML 2.0 organizational SSO and role-based permissions on Teams and Enterprise. Admins manage membership, roles, SSO/security, billing and analytics; Members lack most administrative privileges. Optional Enterprise SCIM automates provisioning with SSO enabled.
    plan_or_license other
  • Has Data retention / training opt-out controls
    Privacy Mode is an actionable settings toggle available even to free and individual users, preventing training on customer data by Cursor and model providers. Teams can enforce it centrally. It is not an unconditional no-storage guarantee: abuse investigations, explicitly approved non-ZDR models, BYOK and Cloud Agent repository storage have documented exceptions.
    other model other other
  • Not found On-premises / private cloud deployment
    No supported deployment of the Cursor service in customer infrastructure or a dedicated private cloud instance was found after checking the relevant official source classes. The current Self-Hosted Machines FAQ explicitly says Cursor is not an on-prem product. Self-hosted workers move only tool execution: Cursor retains the agent loop, inference and planning. CLI deployment to on-prem machines and partner worker integrations have the same cloud dependency, so they do not satisfy the definition. Per-agent isolated VMs, private connectivity, regional residency and customer-managed encryption are scoped controls, not evidence of a dedicated private deployment of the service. Apparent deployment-language conflicts are resolved by this component-level scope; no material deployment access gap remains.
  • Partial IP indemnity / public-code duplication filter
    The current public MSA explicitly indemnifies customers for third-party IP infringement claims involving the Service or any Suggestion, subject to exclusions. Official plan comparison links Teams and Enterprise to the MSA. Only the indemnification branch is confirmed; no built-in public-code duplication blocking setting was established, so the supplied partial criterion applies. Historical forum-based search summaries denying indemnification were not treated as evidence and are superseded by the original current legal text.
    plan_or_license other other
  • Partial Audit logging & usage metrics
    Enterprise customers receive per-event audit logs for authentication, membership, roles, API keys, settings and integrations, exposed through the Admin API. Teams and Enterprise also have administrator-visible usage dashboards and CSV downloads. The supplied partial criterion applies because per-event audit logging and analytics API access are restricted to Enterprise, rather than being generally available across team plans.
    plan_or_license other product_version
  • Uncertain Local / offline (BYO) model support
    Current official governance documentation acknowledges custom models reached via an OpenAI-compatible base URL override. However, the fetched setup guide documents provider API keys, Azure OpenAI and Bedrock, not a supported procedure for connecting a customer-controlled local or self-hosted inference backend. BYOK to a cloud provider alone does not establish the assigned feature. Search summaries offered incompatible interpretations and unverified tunneling workarounds; these were not used as evidence. The available originals do not resolve supported customer-hosted model scope. Offline operation is also not established: all BYOK requests pass through Cursor's backend.
    model other
  • Partial Secret detection & redaction
    Cursor documents automatic redaction for Cloud Agent Runtime Secrets: configured secret values are removed from tool results, chat transcripts, commits and commit messages, and the security overview explicitly says they never reach the model. This establishes a narrow fixed-value protection mechanism, not general discovery of likely credentials in arbitrary code or prompts. Users must designate sensitive values as Runtime Secrets; normal Environment Variables are visible to the agent. Security Review's post-commit secret findings do not establish preventive model-boundary redaction.
    other other
  • Has Agent network egress control / firewall
    Local agent terminal sandboxing has configurable outbound network policy, not merely process isolation. sandbox.json supports default allow/deny, domain and CIDR allowlists, and overriding deny rules; users can select allowlist-only networking and enterprise admins can enforce team networking rules. This finding does not assert that the same configuration governs Cloud Agents or every agent tool.
    platform_or_ide other other
  • Has Data processing / residency region control
    Enterprise customers can enroll individual teams in US-only residency with model inference, content processing and customer-data storage, including backups and Cloud Agents, confined to the US for in-scope features. This is a customer-requested guarantee, not just a default hosting location. Coverage is constrained by model eligibility and excludes external services and BYOK; EU + Iceland coverage is inference-only on request.
    plan_or_license region model other
  • Uncertain Sub-processor / third-party data-sharing disclosure
    The original official security page explicitly states that a subprocessor list is published on Cursor's trust portal, and the DPA identifies that location for updates. First-party ownership of the linked trust subdomain is therefore established. However, access to the actual list was denied by the tool because approval was unavailable. No itemized list was inspected, so the feature's publicly accessible vendor-maintained list criterion cannot be fully verified. This is not classified as partial because the accessible originals claim an itemized list exists, rather than merely offering generic privacy-policy language.
  • Partial Data Processing Agreement (DPA) availability
    A concrete public DPA is available and incorporated into customer contracts. Official help expressly covers Teams and Enterprise customers and excludes individual plans. Classified partial for restricted business-contract availability, rather than suggesting that a privacy policy alone qualifies or that every subscription receives a DPA.
    plan_or_license other
  • Has Encryption in transit & at rest
    Official technical documentation explicitly states encryption both in transit and at rest: TLS 1.2+ for Cursor services and TLS for third-party provider connections, plus AES-256 for stored data, encrypted vector storage and encrypted Cloud Agent code storage.

Additional facts

Built-in tools

  • Bundled tooling:

    Bugbot normally reports findings with a neutral check status. Requiring the check in branch protection therefore ensures a review ran but does not, by itself, block merges on findings. Where fail-on-unresolved-issues behavior is available, it must be enabled to produce a failing status for unresolved findings. This distinction matters when treating automated review as a quality gate.

    • “Requiring the status alone does not block merges on findings because findings default to `neutral`.”
    • “If fail-on-unresolved-issues behavior is available for your organization, enable it to make unresolved findings produce a failing status.”
  • Named sub-agents:

    Cursor documents two built-in subagents: Explore searches and analyzes codebases using a faster model, while Browser controls a browser through MCP tools. Both isolate noisy intermediate work from the parent conversation and return relevant results; custom subagents are a separate user-configurable mechanism.

    • “Cursor includes two built-in subagents that handle context-heavy operations automatically.”
    • “**Explore**”
    • “**Browser**”

Pricing & licensing

  • Plans and availability:

    Automations create Cloud Agents and incur Cloud Agent usage charges. A personal or creator-owned run is billed to that person; a service-account-owned automation is billed to the team's usage pool. Automations use the model's maximum supported context window without a context-window toggle. This is usage-based automation, not an unmetered scheduler entitlement.

    • “Automations create cloud agents and are billed based on cloud agent usage.”
    • “Automations use each model's maximum supported context window because they run as cloud agents. There is no context-window toggle.”
    • “**Service account**: Usage is billed to the team's usage pool.”
  • Pricing:

    Checked on October 11, 2026: the official pricing page's monthly selection displays Pro at US$20/month, Teams Standard at US$40/user/month, and Enterprise at a custom price. Hobby is free with limited Agent requests and access to Composer. These are subscription prices, not a guarantee of unlimited model usage, and prices exclude applicable taxes. No numeric free-tier request allowance or annual price is asserted.

    • “"name":"Pro","price":"20","priceCurrency":"USD"”
    • “"name":"Teams","price":"40","priceCurrency":"USD"”
    • “Limited Agent requests”
    • “All prices are exclusive of any applicable taxes.”
  • Pricing note:

    Pro, Pro Plus, and Ultra have separate Cursor Models and Other Models pools that reset each monthly billing cycle. Third-party model selections draw from Other Models at the model's API rate, with additional usage available for purchase. Start, described as a plan for developers in India, covers Cursor Models but does not include Other Models. Model choice, context size, and parallel subagent work can therefore affect cost independently of subscription price.

    • “There are two separate usage pools, each resetting with your monthly billing cycle:”
    • “When you select a specific third-party model, usage is drawn from the **Other Models** pool at that model's API rate.”
    • “The Start plan does not include this pool.”

Security & data handling

  • Data usage:

    Privacy Mode prevents Cursor training on Customer Data and ordinarily relies on provider zero-data-retention agreements. It is not a universal no-retention promise: abuse-triggered investigations may retain data under provider policies, and non-ZDR models are designated or require administrator opt-in. With Privacy Mode off, Cursor may store and use code, prompts, editor actions, and related data to improve features and train models.

    • “Customer Data will not be used for training by Cursor.”
    • “Non-ZDR models will be designated as such or require an admin to opt-in to enable the model for your workspace.”
    • “we may use and store codebase data, prompts, editor actions, code snippets, and other code data and actions to improve our AI features and train our models.”
  • Data usage:

    Self-Hosted Machines host tool execution, not the Cursor service or inference. The full checkout, build cache, and machine-local credentials stay on the worker, but file contents needed by the agent, terminal output, diffs, screenshots, local MCP results, and routing metadata are sent to Cursor. Artifacts can be uploaded to Cursor-managed storage. Workers require outbound HTTPS; this is neither offline AI operation nor an all-data-stays-local guarantee.

    • “Cursor runs the agent loop, inference, and planning. Your worker performs file edits and terminal commands.”
    • “During a run, the worker sends Cursor the content the agent needs, such as file contents, terminal output, diffs, screenshots, local MCP results, and routing metadata.”
    • “The worker uploads Cloud Agent artifacts, such as screenshots, videos, and log references, to Cursor-managed storage so they can appear in pull requests and the dashboard.”
