DE

devin

Current · researched 2026-10-11T12:47:51Z

Characteristics

Devin is Cognition's coding-agent product family, with materially different Cloud, CLI, and Desktop surfaces. Devin Cloud provides autonomous repository work in a session machine: code generation, coordinated multi-file changes, commands, testing, refactoring, and pull-request creation. Ask Devin provides read-only codebase exploration and an optional plan-to-Agent handoff; it is not the implementation mode. Background Cloud sessions and independent parallel tasks are supported, as is coordinator-led delegation to managed child sessions. These are documented capabilities, not measured guarantees of correctness or delivery speed.

Devin CLI defaults to a local coding agent and has its own permission system, tools, hooks, and subagents; --cloud instead connects to an actual Cloud session. Devin Desktop is the officially documented rebrand of the Windsurf IDE, with current Desktop-specific inline completion and editor generation features. This profile uses that explicit continuity only where supported by current Devin documentation. It does not attribute unrelated legacy Windsurf or Codeium plugin functionality to Cloud.

Access methods

Browser: the merged findings confirm core coding access at app.devin.ai, including Agent sessions and a hosted IDE for monitoring and takeover. Repository indexing, environment setup, account access, and usage allowances apply. The documented mobile-web experience includes session navigation and notifications; mobile_app_access remains partial, not a claim of a verified dedicated iOS/Android app.

Terminal: the standalone CLI is documented for macOS, Linux, WSL, and native Windows. Default sessions run locally; devin --cloud streams a Cloud session working on its own VM. Handoff moves work to Cloud so it can continue after the user's laptop closes. Headless print execution exists, but its merged finding is partial: coding-task completion exit-code semantics were not established, and Cloud print mode can exit while the persistent session continues.

Desktop and other editors: Devin Desktop supplies a full editor and local-agent interface, with current documentation confirming Tab inline completion. Devin CLI integrates through ACP with JetBrains AI Chat, Zed, and Xcode; these are local/CLI integrations, not universal Cloud embedding. Xcode's coding-assistant integration requires 26.6 or later. Teams Desktop access requires a full seat; legacy Desktop subscriptions and Cloud enterprise SKUs should not be treated as interchangeable.

Internal tools and mechanisms

Cloud sessions expose shell, browser, and IDE tools, with clean environment snapshots for new sessions. Ask Devin uses indexed repository context and cited code answers; the merged codebase_semantic_search finding remains uncertain because the required meaning-based retrieval/ranking mechanism was not established. Large-repository handling is supported by concrete context mechanisms rather than an asserted unlimited context window: indexed handoffs, CLI lazy loading of directory instructions, and Security Swarm's task-specific repository partitioning.

Local CLI sessions offer read-only planning, scoped Read/Write/Exec/Fetch/MCP approvals, lifecycle hooks that can block or rewrite actions, and /revert restoration of file and conversation changes from a selected step. That rollback is not a reversal of external side effects. Built-in Explore and General subagents have separate conversation chains and distinct model-selection behavior; background workers cannot request new permissions. Custom worker definitions remain experimental and local-only. Plugin hooks are best-effort and can fail open, so they should not be described as mandatory security controls.

Repository AGENTS.md and rules provide persistent guidance; only the first 16 KiB of each AGENTS.md file is automatically injected. Personal organization-scoped Memory is distinct from shared project instructions and is not used by automation-started sessions. Multiple rule scopes are confirmed, but the merged instruction-precedence finding remains partial: plugin-governance hierarchy does not establish precedence between contradictory instruction texts.

Workflows and use cases

The documented use cases include containerizing a Django service, implementing structured Figma designs through an authorized MCP connection, adding unit/integration coverage, running independent backlog items in parallel, iterating on Review and CI failures with Auto-Fix enabled, and scheduling recurring maintenance through Automations. These examples have different prerequisites and evidence strengths. Figma design-to-code is not proof of generic screenshot-to-new-code generation, and dependency maintenance is not proof of database-backed dependency vulnerability scanning.

A practical Cloud workflow is to explore and scope in Ask Devin, review the generated plan, explicitly send it to Agent mode, and inspect the resulting tests and PR. Plan-first handoff is optional; directly launching Agent mode is also supported. Multi-agent Cloud coordination is distinct from independent parallel sessions and from local CLI workers. Automations support recurring and future one-time runs through RRULE schedules with time zones; legacy Schedules is not the current creation interface.

The locally supervised refactor use case is explicitly inferred from verified planning, permission, testing, refactoring, and rollback capabilities. It is not presented as a separate vendor recipe. Across workflows, scope the task, provide repository conventions and success criteria, and review outputs rather than interpreting autonomy as a correctness guarantee.

Integrations

The merged native integration catalog names GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps, Slack, Microsoft Teams, Jira, Linear, PagerDuty, and Pylon, with additional Databricks and MongoDB connection guides. This is a documented set, not an exhaustive integration count. Native connections, MCP servers, and plugin packages are separate mechanisms; installation does not automatically authorize access to external services. Custom Cloud MCP supports STDIO, SSE, and HTTP and requires the appropriate management permission and credentials.

Provider capabilities and entitlements differ. GitLab Self-Managed support is Enterprise-scoped and documents version 15.0 or later; Azure DevOps setup directs users to an Enterprise account; Pylon is catalogued as beta. Devin Review supports provider-specific PR review, but Bitbucket Data Center requires 8.16 or later and Bitbucket Cloud is not supported by Review. GitHub Review write actions require the GitHub App connection; PAT-based access is read-only. Repository PR creation support must not be confused with identical Review support across providers.

MCP extensibility is confirmed. Native non-MCP callable-tool registration remains uncertain; skills, plugin hooks, workflow scripts, and changelog mentions of scripted tools do not by themselves establish that interface.

Security

The merged findings confirm encrypted transit/storage, Enterprise SAML/OIDC SSO and granular RBAC, and Cloud security profiles with destination allowlists. Enterprise event-level audit logging is verified but rated partial under the assigned enterprise-tier criterion. Cloud security profiles govern network, git, MCP, and integration access; CLI per-action approvals are a different control system. Customer-managed Outposts must enforce their published network policy themselves.

Cloud sessions use isolated execution machines. CLI OS sandboxing is a Research Preview, is unsupported on native Windows, and has separate Linux dependencies. Its network filtering is documented as unstable; direct edit/write tools operate outside the command-process sandbox. Bypass or reduced-interruption modes do not override organization-enforced deny/ask rules. These limitations should remain visible in deployment decisions.

Paid-plan Data Controls opt-out disables training and enables ZDR with model providers; Teams requires an administrator, while Enterprise training requires prior written consent. This is not blanket zero retention at Cognition. A public DPA is available. Core processing locations in its tables are United States-based, with India support processing also listed; this does not establish exclusive geographic residency. Customer Dedicated hosting is Cognition-managed, and Outposts moves execution to customer infrastructure while inference/planning remains in Devin Cloud.

Subprocessor disclosure is confirmed as has in the refreshed merged findings: the public DPA identifies Appendix C as its current named roster with purposes and locations. Its scope is Customer Data processed under the applicable customer agreement, excluding Account Data, rather than every supplier processing every customer's data. The second table applies to Personal Data submitted as Input; starred Databricks, xAI, and Snowflake entries apply only if enabled in Devin Desktop and do not establish Cloud suppliers. Verification of this public roster does not require gated access. Detailed Trust Center security documents still require access approval and an NDA and were not inspected. Saved-secret output masking is documented, but unregistered-secret detection before inference or disk writes remains uncertain. Enterprise attribution filtering is partial, support-enabled, and not evidence of generated-output IP indemnity.

Constraints

Evidence gaps: the canonical homepage and pricing page both returned HTTP 404 on October 11, 2026. Current self-serve documentation lists Pro at $20/month, Max at $200/month, and Teams at an $80/month minimum with $40/month full seats, but these prices could not be checked against the page the documentation calls authoritative. Exact numerical quotas and a complete cross-plan feature matrix were not established. NDA-gated Trust Center resources and private enterprise commitments were not accessed.

Do not promote uncertain findings: meaning-based semantic retrieval, native non-MCP custom-tool registration, dependency-to-CVE scanning, pre-disk-write diff acceptance, generic image-to-new-code generation, unregistered-secret scanning, customer-controlled inference backends, and full zero-network operation remain uncertain in the supplied merged results. Desktop per-hunk accept/reject controls do not settle when edits reach disk. Federal air-gapped CLI/Desktop statements and diagnostic commands do not establish generally available zero-connectivity operation. Cloud dedicated hosting and Outposts are not offline inference.

Cost and scope: parallel sessions and workers add usage. Teams Automations and AI Review draw from shared on-demand credits; exhausting credits stops Automations and removes AI Review while retaining the smart diff viewer. Full seats include Desktop, flex seats do not. Legacy Desktop wording about dollar-valued usage should not override current self-serve quota mechanics. Custom subagents are experimental; Cloud/local tools and permission rules are not interchangeable. The public DPA roster confirms subprocessor disclosure, not universal supplier applicability; its starred Databricks, xAI, and Snowflake entries are conditional on Devin Desktop enablement, not evidence of Cloud use.

Review and history: generated code can contain bugs or insecure behavior; preserve human review, tests, and branch protections. The release-history entries are a selected, official-changelog-backed set newer than the June 24, 2026 cutoff, not a complete enumeration of every intervening Cloud, CLI, or Desktop release. No Desktop-only release history was verified here.

Use cases

  • Containerize and verify a Django service Documented

    Documented Devin Cloud example: generate coordinated Docker and Compose configuration for Django, PostgreSQL, and Redis, then build and run the stack. Repository access and a working execution environment are prerequisites; the example is not a guarantee that every application will containerize successfully.

  • Implement a design through Figma MCP Documented

    Connect a Figma account authorized for the design, extract structured design information, build components, and visually compare the result with mockups. This is a documented design-to-code integration workflow, not proof of generic raster image-to-new-code generation.

  • Perform a locally supervised refactor Inferred

    An inferred workflow combines read-only CLI planning, explicit command/write permissions, repository tests, and step-based rollback for a bounded local refactor. Rollback covers documented file and conversation changes, not remote deployments or other external effects.

    Why inferred: The merged results establish plan-only operation, granular action approvals, instruction-driven refactoring, test generation, and CLI step rollback. Combining them suggests a supervised workflow, but the combined sequence is not asserted as a separately vendor-documented recipe.

  • Work through independent backlog items in parallel Documented

    Split independent work into separate Cloud sessions and return to draft PRs for review. Keep this distinct from one coordinator delegating parts of a shared task. Concurrent work consumes additional usage; no numeric session-concurrency limit was established.

    • “Carve out independent tasks and run them simultaneously.”
    • “Return to draft PRs waiting for review.”
  • Schedule recurring maintenance Documented

    Use Automations Schedule triggers for recurring error triage, dependency updates, or reports. Current scheduling uses Automations rather than the legacy Schedules interface. Teams runs require shared on-demand credits; upgrading dependencies is not evidence of dependency-to-CVE scanning.

  • Iterate on review findings and failing CI Documented

    Enable Devin Review with Auto-Fix and grant the repository integration's required permissions so Devin can respond to findings and CI failures. Human review and branch protection remain appropriate; automatic recovery is a configured workflow, not an unconditional correctness guarantee.

  • Add targeted unit and integration coverage Documented

    Use the vendor's test-coverage template to target a file, module, or function, follow existing testing patterns, and run the tests against an explicit coverage goal. The example command is npm-based, not a documented product-wide language restriction.

The official FAQ explicitly identifies the Windsurf-to-Devin Desktop rebrand, so this finding is not an attribution of unrelated Windsurf plugin functionality to Devin Cloud. The Cloud session IDE also lists Tab autocomplete, but the detailed confirmation here rests on current Desktop documentation.

Mobile app development/emulator support and third-party Slack/Teams applications are not evidence for a dedicated Devin mobile app. This partial rating is for documented mobile web only, not a native-app claim; inaccessible marketing pages prevent an exhaustive native-app absence finding.
    platform_or_ide
  • Partial Headless / non-interactive CI mode
    Devin CLI documents non-interactive --print execution, ATIF conversation export, bypass permission mode, and skipping workspace trust checks for scripts/CI. Cloud Devin also has an explicit --cloud -p mode, but it prints a response and exits while the cloud session persists; that is not a documented completion-based CI success signal. The checked reference documents non-zero status for doctor diagnostics, not coding-task exit-code semantics. Accordingly the unattended CLI surface is real, but the full structured-output-and-meaningful-task-exit-code criterion is not established. Hook or diagnostic exit codes and AI-search assertions about standard CLI conventions were not treated as task-execution evidence.
    other other other plan_or_license
  • Uncertain Full offline operation
    No current zero-network operating mode was established for Devin Cloud. Enterprise deployment documentation says the brain remains in Cognition's cloud, and Outposts explicitly retains cloud inference even on customer machines. Separately, the federal FAQ says fully air-gapped Devin CLI/Desktop versions are being finalized, while the CLI reference already mentions air-gapped builds and model endpoint connectivity. These are scope differences, not evidence that the whole Devin product currently works without any network. Air-gapped operation can still require an internal network to model endpoints; no available page establishes zero connectivity, availability, or the full core-functionality coverage of that special build. Therefore neither has nor partial is substantiated, and a complete negative finding would be inappropriate.
    other release_stage product_version

Security & Governance

  • Has Enterprise SSO / access control
    Devin Enterprise documents SAML 2.0 and OIDC identity-provider connections alongside configurable organization- and account-level roles and fine-grained permissions. Roles can be assigned to individual users and IdP groups. This meets both SSO and RBAC criteria, not merely team membership.
    plan_or_license integration_required other
  • Has Data retention / training opt-out controls
    The Devin security page describes an actionable Data Controls training opt-out for paid plans, enabling Zero Data Retention with model providers after opting out. This is not enterprise-only: Pro, Max and Teams are paid self-serve plans. Enterprise data is not used for training without prior written consent. Scope resolves the apparent difference between general default training language and enterprise no-training language.
    plan_or_license other other
  • Has On-premises / private cloud deployment
    Devin Enterprise offers a supported Customer Dedicated Deployment in a customer-isolated single-tenant VPC, meeting the dedicated private deployment criterion without relying on a differently branded product. Cognition manages this environment; it is not a fully offline deployment of Devin's brain. Outposts separately permits customer-operated execution infrastructure while retaining cloud inference. Federal air-gapped Desktop/CLI statements were not treated as a released full on-premises Cloud service.
    plan_or_license other integration_required plan_or_license other

    Devin Enterprise offers support-enabled public-code attribution filtering for cloud file-editing tools and Devin CLI. Partial follows the assigned criteria because this is enterprise-only, with no self-serve toggle, and generated-output IP indemnification was not established. The public MSA's service indemnity excludes Customer Data, whose definition includes Outputs; it is not evidence of indemnifying generated code. Ownership of output alone is also insufficient.

    Enterprise administrators have event-level audit logs via API, including login, session lifecycle, role, settings and security-profile actions, plus consumption reporting. Organization usage metrics are also documented. Partial follows the assigned criterion for logging limited to an enterprise tier; it does not mean the available enterprise logs are merely aggregate.

    No supported configuration for a customer-controlled local/self-hosted inference backend was verified. Devin Cloud explicitly rejects third-party LLM API keys and retains its brain in Cognition Cloud; Outposts moves execution, not inference, onto customer machines. CLI model selection is not evidence of a custom backend. Federal documentation mentions private team models but does not explain their ownership, hosting, or endpoint configuration, and describes fully air-gapped Desktop/CLI versions as being finalized. These narrower statements do not prove a product-wide absence or establish customer model control. Search summaries asserting Ollama support without URLs were excluded. Neither establishes detection of likely unregistered credentials in code/context before inference or disk writes. AI Guardrails addresses prompt injection, exfiltration requests and policy violations without explicitly documenting credential scanning. Additional facts

Built-in tools

  • Named sub-agents:

    Devin CLI has two built-in worker profiles: subagent_explore for read-only exploration and research, and subagent_general for general work including code changes. Explore uses a router-selected or configured default subagent model; General follows the parent's model. Background workers cannot obtain new approvals and use only pre-approved tools. Each worker incurs its own inference usage. User-defined profiles are experimental and apply to local agents, not Cloud sessions.

    • “Each subagent runs with a specific profile that determines its capabilities. There are two built-in profiles:”
    • “`subagent_general` inherits the parent's model.”
    • “Background subagents cannot prompt you for new permissions.”
    • “Custom subagents are **experimental**.”

Pricing & licensing

  • Plans and availability:

    The official Desktop FAQ identifies Devin Desktop as the renamed Windsurf IDE and describes Devin Local as using the same architecture as Devin CLI. This supports attribution of current Devin Desktop documentation, not blanket transfer of legacy Windsurf plugin claims to Cloud. Legacy Desktop arrangements can remain separate from the Cloud SKU; current self-serve Teams Desktop access requires a full seat. The FAQ's older dollar-valued usage wording is not used to override the current billing page's quota description.

    • “Devin Desktop is the new name for Windsurf.”
    • “Devin Cloud remains a separate SKU.”
    • “It's more efficient than Cascade, supports subagents, and runs the same architecture as Devin CLI.”
  • Plans & pricing:

    Official self-serve billing documentation lists Free, Pro at $20/month, Max at $200/month, and Teams with an $80/month minimum and up to 200 members. Teams full seats cost $40/month each; flex seats have no fixed seat charge and use shared on-demand credits, but do not include Desktop access. Pro and Max are single-user plans. These are documentation-listed prices, not independently confirmed against the canonical pricing page: https://devin.ai/pricing returned HTTP 404 on October 11, 2026.

    • “| **Pro** | Individual users | \$20/month | 1 | | **Max** | Power users who need more quota | \$200/month | 1 | | **Teams** | Teams working with Devin together | \$80/month minimum | Up to 200 |”
    • “**\$40/month per seat**, billed as a fixed recurring line item.”
    • “* Do **not** include Devin Desktop access”
  • Pricing:

    Pro and Teams full seats have daily and weekly usage allowances; Max has a larger weekly allowance without a daily cap. Individual allowances cover Cloud sessions, CLI, and Desktop. Purchased on-demand credits roll over and never expire. Teams Automations and AI Review consume shared on-demand credits rather than full-seat quota; without credits, Automations stop and Review falls back to its smart diff viewer. Exact numerical allowances are not specified in the fetched billing page.

    • “* **Max** has a **weekly** allowance only, with no daily cap.”

Security & data handling

  • Data usage:

    The public Cognition DPA explicitly identifies Appendix C as its current subprocessor list and supplies named entities, purposes, and locations, supporting the refreshed sub_processor_disclosure finding of has. The DPA covers Customer Data processed on the customer's behalf through Cognition's enterprise or software services under the applicable customer agreement, excluding Account Data; the roster does not establish that every supplier processes every customer's data. Core processing rows include United States locations, while an India support-workflow row is also present. A separate model-provider table applies to the extent Personal Data is submitted as Input to the Services. Its starred Databricks, xAI, and Snowflake entries apply only if enabled in Devin Desktop and must not be imported into Cloud claims.

    The public Cognition Trust Center landing page is accessible, but detailed security resources require requested access and a signed NDA. Those resources were not accessed. This restriction does not make the separately public DPA or security overview unavailable.

    Paid customers can opt out of model training through Data Controls, with model-provider Zero Data Retention enabled afterward; Teams requires an administrator. Enterprise data requires express prior written consent for training. Provider ZDR is not a promise that Cognition stores no customer or session data: the same security page describes retention during the customer relationship and separate feedback/interaction retention.

GI

GitHub Copilot

Current · researched 2026-10-11T12:32:21Z

Characteristics

GitHub Copilot combines interactive coding assistance with agent-driven development across editors, a standalone terminal agent, GitHub.com, mobile, and a dedicated desktop app. The supplied merged findings establish inline completion, natural-language and multi-file generation, test generation, refactoring, image-derived code generation, and dedicated pull-request review. These are different workflows, not interchangeable names for one chat interface.

IDE agent mode can inspect a project, select files, edit code, run commands, and iterate on validation failures. CLI adds explicit planning, configurable tool permissions, autonomous continuation, custom agents, and coordinated subagents. Cloud agent performs delegated repository work asynchronously and can prepare a pull request for human review. Independent app sessions use separate branches/worktrees; CLI /fleet instead coordinates subtasks within one request. Neither concurrency mechanism guarantees faster or correct results.

This profile synthesizes the supplied final feature records without changing their statuses. The current source checks and release capture are dated October 11, 2026. Product-level has findings should be read with their client, plan, model, policy, and release-stage constraints, not as feature parity across every Copilot surface.

Access methods

Use Copilot in an IDE for inline suggestions and interactive chat/agent work. The merged matrix lists completion in VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains, Eclipse, Xcode, and NeoVim; NeoVim does not have the same chat, agent-mode, or MCP support. Install a supported integration and sign in with the appropriate account. The October 10 JetBrains announcement now requires IDE 2025.2 or later; older general compatibility information is not sufficient for the latest plugin.

Copilot CLI runs independently of an IDE on Linux, macOS, and Windows through PowerShell or WSL. It supports interactive conversations and a programmatic prompt-and-exit interface. The npm installation channel requires Node.js 22+, while standalone executables and other channels are also documented. Plan before editing in interactive plan mode, or configure authentication and narrowly scoped permissions for unattended work. Local BYOK is a distinct access path: the merged findings establish that it does not require a Copilot subscription, while hosted Copilot usage depends on entitlement and policies.

GitHub.com provides browser chat, repository questions, review, and cloud-agent delegation without a local IDE. Cloud agent works with GitHub-hosted repositories, not arbitrary hosting platforms. GitHub Mobile supplies official Android/iOS chat access, not a mobile code editor. The Copilot app runs on macOS, Linux, and Windows and coordinates parallel repository work; the current plans page includes both app and CLI in all plans, with usage and administrator controls still applying. The surface guide also identifies SDK-powered custom applications and GitHub Desktop commit-message assistance; those are separate access methods, not full IDE equivalents.

Internal tools and mechanisms

The merged findings establish file inspection/editing, terminal command execution, Git operations, repository semantic retrieval, and validation-driven iteration. Repository indexing enriches GitHub/VS Code Chat and cloud-agent context; it should not be generalized to every IDE. Non-GitHub workspace indexing in VS Code uploads workspace data to GitHub and requires the applicable policy enablement. CLI manages long sessions by compacting history into summaries, preserving instructions and plan state but losing fine detail. The dedicated context-management page describes background compaction around 80% and a pause near 95% if needed; this is not unlimited verbatim memory.

CLI has named explore, task, general-purpose, code-review, research, rubber-duck, and security-review specialists. Custom Markdown/YAML profiles can specify prompts and tools; subagents have separate context windows. /fleet can coordinate dependencies and parallel work where suitable, potentially increasing credit consumption. The task specialist runs available project build/test/lint/format commands; this does not substantiate a universally bundled formatter or linter.

Repository instructions persist across requests, but supported scopes and instruction formats differ by client. The verified personal/repository/organization precedence belongs to GitHub.com, not every IDE or CLI session. Repository JSON hooks for CLI/cloud agent can run at lifecycle and tool-use events, including approval/denial before tool use. SDK custom tools and experimental JavaScript CLI extensions provide native callable-tool registration in their respective surfaces. Experimental extensions and opt-in planning should not be presented as mandatory behavior for all requests.

Workflows and use cases

Documented workflows include understanding unfamiliar code, generating new files or project scaffolds, repairing/refactoring existing code, and writing tests for selected code with framework and edge-case instructions. Image-to-code examples use UI mockups or screenshots in supported IDE Chat clients with an image-capable model; the merged matrix retains client-specific preview markers. Generated code and tests still need execution and review.

A terminal issue-to-PR workflow can begin with an issue URL, proceed through an implementation plan and permitted edits/commands, and create a GitHub pull request. Cloud agent instead researches, plans, and implements delegated work in the background. It operates on one repository and branch, can open one PR per task, and has a 59-minute maximum session runtime. Humans should review output before merging; Actions workflows on agent pull requests require approval by default.

Native automations support recurring hourly/daily/weekly schedules and repository-event triggers. Official examples include issue triage, nightly failing-test repair attempts, and weekly release-note drafts. They require private/internal repositories, write access, enabled policies, and an eligible paid plan. Automations are not stored/versioned in Git; their sessions and logs are visible to repository readers even though configuration is private to the creator.

For automation outside that UI, the merged headless finding is specifically grounded in CLI programmatic interfaces, JSONL output, and a direct dynamic-workflow mode with documented exit codes. Its workflow registration/trust requirements and exit-code table must not be assumed to cover every ordinary -p invocation. Parallel modernization is an inferred combined workflow using independent app sessions, /fleet, tests, and PR review; it is not a documented performance claim.

Integrations

The supplied official integration catalog establishes cloud-agent integrations with Microsoft Teams, Slack, Linear, Azure Boards, and Jira. These bring conversation, issue, or work-item context into GitHub repository changes and pull requests. The count describes that catalog, not every possible plugin or MCP connector. Teams and Slack remain public preview and require app installation, account linking, repository permissions, and enabled cloud sandboxes. Linear setup requires the appropriate GitHub/Linear administration; Azure Boards requires its GitHub app and project authorization; Jira requires Jira Cloud AI/Rovo and both application installations. Enterprise data-residency installations can use separate GHE.com routes.

MCP is the broader extensibility mechanism. CLI supports local and remote servers, the app can reuse repository/CLI configuration, and repository settings serve cloud agent and code review. GitHub and Playwright servers are documented defaults in those GitHub.com agent/review workflows. Local/remote transports and authentication vary by client, and Business/Enterprise MCP policy is disabled by default. Registry listings from partners or the community are discoverable extensions, not automatic endorsements or universal compatibility guarantees.

The October 2 code-review announcement additionally establishes GA REST/GraphQL review requests with per-request effort selection for paid plans. Native SDK tools and experimental CLI extensions are distinct from MCP and from the five cloud-agent catalog integrations.

Security

Security controls are scope-specific. CLI can allow/deny tool categories, shell subcommands, and paths; deny rules override allows. Autonomous continuation does not remove permission requirements. VS Code can show a diff and request approval before configured file edits, whereas ordinary pending Keep/Undo changes are already saved. Agent Host has a different review state, and pre-apply edit approval does not prove interception of arbitrary script or terminal writes. Checkpoints/CLI rewind restore tracked workspace changes and conversation state within documented limits, not deployments, network calls, or other external side effects.

Local sandboxing reached GA on October 7 in CLI, the app, and VS Code Agent Host sessions. It is included at no extra charge and uses native OS containment; the merged documentation notes opt-in defaults, OS differences, and best-effort handling for in-process file tools. Cloud sandboxes remain separately documented public preview, usage-billed, and restricted to supported interactive CLI sessions. Tool isolation is not model/data-location isolation. Cloud agent also has a configurable egress firewall with organization/repository allowlists, but its Bash-process boundary does not cover every MCP/setup process and GitHub warns of bypass risk.

Cloud-agent generated-code validation integrates CodeQL, secret scanning, and new-dependency checks against the Advisory Database for malware and High/Critical vulnerabilities; administrators can disable validation. Supported remote GitHub MCP push protection can block secrets in mediated responses/actions, subject to repository security coverage and bypass rules. This is not universal pre-inference prompt redaction or prevention of every local write. The October 7 secret-classifier announcement explicitly separates existing alerts from future opt-in Copilot checks; coming-soon/private-preview capabilities are not asserted as generally available.

Business/Enterprise governance includes SSO/identity-provider integration, granular policy roles, audit events, and exportable usage reports. Training opt-out differs between individual and organizational plans and is not zero retention. The merged DPA finding remains organizational/GA-and-covered-preview scoped; public-code filtering is verified but output legal defense depends on the customer's agreement and mitigations. HTTPS transit encryption is verified; at-rest encryption remains unverified because the supplied research had material Trust Center access gaps. Enterprise data-residency controls can restrict inference to certified US/EU models when explicitly enabled, with compatible clients and a 10% credit overhead; they are not a default global guarantee.

Constraints

As checked October 11, plans include Free, verified Student, Pro, Pro+, Max, Business, and Enterprise. Published monthly prices are USD 10/39/100 for Pro/Pro+/Max and USD 19/39 per granted seat for Business/Enterprise. Current allowances are AI-credit based: paid individual totals include both base and flex amounts (1,500/7,000/20,000 respectively), while Business/Enterprise list 1,900/3,900 per user/month. Free has 2,000 inline completions/month and limited agents; Free/Student use auto model selection. These are current checked values, not historical premium-request quotas. Model access, additional paid usage, cloud sandbox costs, Actions consumption, and organization policies can further constrain work.

Model support changes over time. Haiku 5.5 was announced GA October 7 for paid plans with gradual rollout and policy controls. The October 2 deprecation notice removes Gemini 3.5/3.6 Flash, Kimi K2.7 Code, and Claude Opus 4.7; historical availability posts should not override it. Image input requires a capable model, code review does not offer ordinary user model switching, and residency restrictions narrow the usable model set. CLI extensions and certain IDE/BYOK or vision experiences retain their documented experimental/preview scope. Cloud sandboxes and Teams/Slack previews must not be conflated with CLI or local sandbox GA.

The supplied full offline operation and on-premises/private deployment records remain uncertain. CLI local-provider offline mode is separately documented: it prevents GitHub contact only when explicitly configured, and complete network isolation also requires a local/isolated provider. Merely selecting Ollama neither enables offline mode nor disables telemetry. This narrower supported path does not prove every Copilot surface works offline or that the Copilot service can be self-hosted. Self-hosted Actions runners relocate agent execution infrastructure, not the entire service. GitHub Enterprise Server remains explicitly unsupported for Copilot; the planned GHES security-alert model is a different product capability.

Usage reports also have quality limits. Besides telemetry, client-version, and reporting-delay requirements in the merged findings, the October 6 notice identifies SDK-based IDE agent attribution loss and historical CLI inflation. VS Code 1.139.0+ has a fix; other IDE fixes were expected later, and missing data cannot be backfilled. General minimum telemetry versions do not establish complete agent reporting. The profile records these newer caveats and scope tensions without rewriting the final merged feature statuses.

Use cases

  • Generate framework-specific tests Documented

    Use /tests on existing code in supported IDE Chat clients, naming a framework or edge case. For test-driven development, describe intended behavior without /tests. Review and run the resulting tests; generation is not evidence of their correctness or coverage.

    • “Use the `/tests` slash command to ask Copilot to write tests for the active file or selected code.”
    • “`/tests using the Jest framework`”
    • “If you prefer to write tests before writing code (test driven development), omit the `/tests` command.”
  • Parallelize a reviewed modernization effort Inferred

    A team could divide separable modernization tasks into isolated app sessions, use CLI /fleet for independent subtasks within a session, and route resulting changes through tests and pull-request review. Dependency ordering, model cost, permissions, and human review remain necessary; speed or correctness gains are not guaranteed.

    Why inferred: The merged findings establish independent sessions on separate branches/worktrees, coordinated CLI subagents, multi-location refactoring, test generation, and GitHub pull-request workflows. Combining these mechanisms suggests this workflow; no vendor case study or measured outcome is asserted.

  • Schedule repository maintenance Documented

    Use native automations for issue triage, nightly attempts to repair failing tests, or weekly release-note drafts. Configure recurring or repository-event triggers and only the necessary tools. Private/internal repositories, write access, eligible paid plans, policies, and creator-billed usage constrain this workflow.

    • “**Fix failing tests nightly**: each night, check for failing tests on the `main` branch, attempt a fix, and open a draft pull request.”
    • “**Prepare weekly release notes**: draft release notes and open a pull request on a schedule.”
  • Implement an issue from the terminal Documented

    Give CLI an issue or repository change request, ask it to work on a named branch, and create a GitHub pull request. Interactive plan mode can establish scope before code is written; tool permissions determine whether commands and writes can proceed. This is a GitHub workflow, not a verified GitLab merge-request integration.

    • “Ask Copilot to work on an issue:”
    • “Ask Copilot to make file changes and raise a pull request on GitHub.com.”
    • “In plan mode, Copilot analyzes your request, asks clarifying questions to understand scope and requirements, and builds a plan before writing any code.”
  • Explore an unfamiliar codebase Documented

    Ask IDE Chat about algorithms, relationships between files, or how project features work, supplying selected code, file references, or workspace context. CLI can delegate codebase exploration to a read-only specialist. Repository semantic indexing is separately verified for GitHub/VS Code Chat and cloud agent, not every editor.

Features

Code Authoring & Editing

  • Has Inline code completion
    Copilot automatically generates grayed inline suggestions as the developer types, including complete function bodies, without a chat prompt. Current IDE documentation describes partial-line, whole-line, and larger-block suggestions. The feature matrix lists completion support in VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains, Eclipse, Xcode, and NeoVim. Numerous languages are supported rather than a documented narrow language subset.
    plan_or_license platform_or_ide product_version
  • Has Natural-language-to-code generation
    Official examples range from requesting a function in chat to creating complete multi-file projects. The IDE quickstart asks the user to describe a task-manager web application in Agent mode and states that Copilot generates the needed files and code. This is new code generated from a natural-language instruction rather than completion of an already typed function header. Generated applications still require review and validation; documentation is not proof that every generated output will run correctly.
    platform_or_ide plan_or_license model other
  • Has Multi-file code generation
    A single high-level task in agent mode generates the required files and code, with Copilot deciding which files to change. The project scaffolding examples also provide a directory structure and a control to create the suggested files and contents. The refactoring example demonstrates coordinated new and revised files from one instruction. No manual re-invocation per file is required.
    platform_or_ide product_version plan_or_license other
  • Has Automated refactoring
    An official worked example uses a single project-level natural-language refactoring prompt to centralize logging, create a logging aspect, update main.py, and remove duplicated logging from multiple service classes. The documented result preserves the logging operations while restructuring their implementation. This is AI-driven multi-location restructuring, not merely a symbol rename or an IDE-native command; correctness of any particular generated refactor still needs testing.
    platform_or_ide other
  • Has Diff review and selective apply
    VS Code documents an opt-in edit approval workflow that displays a diff and asks for approval or rejection before an edit is applied. This meets the strict pre-write requirement when the relevant paths require approval. Separate Local-harness review supports individual inline edits, rather than only whole files. However ordinary pending Keep/Undo edits are already saved, and Agent Host applies edits directly, so those default post-write workflows alone do not qualify. The status is scoped to the configurable pre-apply approval workflow, not all Copilot surfaces.
    platform_or_ide other other
  • Has Multimodal input (image/screenshot to code)
    The official IDE Chat guide explicitly documents attaching a UI mockup to generate application code and attaching a web-page screenshot to generate similar HTML. These examples establish image-derived code generation, not only image explanation. Image attachments are supported on all Copilot plans, but require an image-capable model and a supporting client.
    model platform_or_ide release_stage plan_or_license other

Agentic Execution & Runtime

  • Has Autonomous multi-step task execution
    Copilot CLI autopilot carries out successive task steps without waiting for further user instructions. IDE agent mode independently selects files, edits them, executes commands and iterates; cloud agent plans and implements delegated tasks. This is general multi-step execution, not a fixed predefined workflow.
    other platform_or_ide plan_or_license
  • Has Background / long-running task execution
    Cloud agent researches, plans and implements delegated changes in the background while the user continues working. It requests review when coding work finishes. This satisfies asynchronous task execution independently of narrow background test or terminal-command support.
    platform_or_ide other other
  • Has Terminal command execution
    IDE agent mode and Copilot CLI execute shell commands directly, rather than requiring copy/paste. The VS Code terminal tool exposes output to chat and feeds execution results into the agent loop. Default approvals can be granted per invocation or for session tools, and CLI command-line allow/deny controls support noninteractive execution.
    other platform_or_ide other
  • Has Sandboxed / isolated execution environment
    Copilot documents both opt-in OS-level local sandboxing and fully isolated ephemeral Linux cloud sandboxes for CLI and app sessions. Because local sandboxing is available in addition to cloud-only execution and is not restricted to a specific paid plan, the feature is not limited to the definition's cloud-only partial case. Local containment is explicitly lighter-weight than a VM or container; cloud execution provides the stronger environment isolation.
    other platform_or_ide release_stage plan_or_license
  • Has Parallel independent task execution
    The Copilot app explicitly supports concurrent independent agent sessions with dedicated branches and worktrees, with a single interface for directing them. GitHub agent management also documents concurrent sessions. This is supported independent task concurrency, not merely /fleet subagents completing parts of one request or manually launching unrelated application instances.
    platform_or_ide plan_or_license
  • Has Self-healing error recovery
    Copilot IDE agent mode is documented as iterating to remediate issues until the original task is complete. The first-party VS Code agent-loop documentation specifies the missing operational detail: after editing code and tests, the agent runs tests, diagnoses failed validation, changes code again and validates again within the same task. This is an autonomous failure-detection/fix/retest loop, not a guarantee that every failure will be solved.
    platform_or_ide other
  • Has Agent session checkpoint & rollback
    VS Code documents a checkpoint restore that reverts affected workspace files and conversation history across subsequent requests in one operation, rather than requiring per-file or per-hunk undo. CLI also offers prompt-level conversation-and-files rewind across later turns. This is session-wide rollback of tracked agent work, not reversal of external side effects or an unrestricted machine snapshot. An inconsistent warning in the CLI concept page does not establish broader restoration coverage; the operational how-to and VS Code checkpoint documentation substantiate the narrower supported scope.
    platform_or_ide other other
  • Has Scheduled / recurring task execution
    Native Copilot automations let a user save a prompt and choose a recurring hourly, daily or weekly schedule that starts cloud agent without a new interactive prompt. Configuration is provided through GitHub's repository Agents tab or the Copilot app, so this does not depend on an external third-party cron trigger. A recurring schedule suffices for the has criterion; a one-time future trigger is not claimed.
    plan_or_license platform_or_ide other

Agent Customization & Orchestration

  • Has Multi-agent / sub-agent orchestration
    Copilot CLI documents main-agent delegation to built-in and user-defined subagents. The /fleet command explicitly decomposes requests, coordinates subtask dependencies, and runs agents in parallel when suitable. This is orchestration rather than manually starting independent sessions.
    platform_or_ide other model plan_or_license
  • Has User-defined sub-agent roles
    Users can author Markdown/YAML custom agent profiles with independent prompts and tool allowlists, optionally including MCP server configuration. The documented CLI /agent creation flow explicitly permits restricting tools, and custom profiles can be instantiated as subagents with separate context windows.

  • Has Custom tool / function-calling API
    Official documentation provides native non-MCP registration surfaces: the Copilot SDK defines callable tools with argument schemas and handlers and passes them through session tools configuration. Copilot CLI extensions can also register tools into an existing interactive session through joinSession. This satisfies the documented API/config criterion; the CLI extension surface is explicitly experimental, not undocumented.
    platform_or_ide release_stage other integration_required other
  • Has Agent lifecycle hooks
    GitHub documents repository-configured JSON hooks that execute user-supplied shell commands at session, prompt, pre-tool, post-tool, and agent-stop events. The preToolUse hook can approve or deny any tool execution, meeting the action-influence criterion rather than merely sending passive notifications.
    platform_or_ide other
  • Has Permission / autonomy-level granularity
    Copilot CLI permissions independently allow or deny tool kinds, including shell commands, read operations, and writes. Rules can further scope shell subcommands and individual paths, allowing selected actions without prompts while leaving other categories subject to approval. Tool availability controls are separate from permission controls.

  • Has Plan visibility before execution
    Copilot CLI has an explicit plan mode for collaborating on an implementation plan before code is written. Its documented workflow presents an Accept plan option before continuing into autonomous execution, including an optional /fleet execution choice.

Context & Code Quality

  • Has Codebase-wide semantic search
    Repository semantic indexing is explicitly used to answer natural-language codebase questions with relevant code references. Cloud agent also automatically retrieves code by meaning rather than exact grep matches. This establishes repository-wide semantic retrieval, not merely substring search or active-file context.
    platform_or_ide platform_or_ide other
  • Has Large-repository / long-context handling
    Copilot documents codebase-specific semantic retrieval from repository indexes, including background indexing for large repositories, and CLI conversation compaction for long sessions. Compaction summarizes goals, technical details, important files, and next steps while retaining original instructions and plan state. These are concrete repository/session context-management mechanisms rather than a bare model context-window claim.
    platform_or_ide model other plan_or_license
  • Has Persistent project memory / custom instructions
    Repository-scoped custom instructions are persisted in .github/copilot-instructions.md, with optional path-specific and agent files. They automatically provide repository context on subsequent requests rather than requiring users to paste guidance into each new conversation. This meets persistent project instructions without relying on session-only compaction or separately assessing Copilot Memory.
    platform_or_ide other other
  • Has Automated test generation
    Official IDE guidance explicitly documents /tests generating tests for an active file or selected code, with optional framework and edge-case instructions. It also documents test-first generation for code that has not yet been written. This is a named test-generation capability rather than incidental general code generation.
    platform_or_ide plan_or_license
  • Has Automated code review / PR review
    Copilot has a dedicated review product that analyzes pull requests and suggests fixes, not merely an ad hoc chat request. Automatic PR reviews can be configured by users, repository owners, or organization owners. The PR-hosting workflow meets the full criterion.
    plan_or_license platform_or_ide release_stage model integration_required other
  • Has Static analysis / linting integration
    Copilot cloud agent runs CodeQL security static analysis on generated code and attempts to resolve identified issues before completing its PR. Analysis and remediation are visible in session logs. This establishes analyzer findings influencing AI changes, beyond an editor merely displaying lint diagnostics; the claim does not imply a bundled style linter in every Copilot surface.
    platform_or_ide plan_or_license other
  • Has Dependency vulnerability scanning (SCA)
    Cloud agent has documented built-in dependency validation against the GitHub Advisory Database, with analysis and actions visible in its session log and identified issues fed back into remediation. This meets the database-backed integration criterion. The confirmed scope is newly introduced dependencies and malware/High/Critical findings, not an assertion that every existing dependency or vulnerability severity is scanned continuously.
    platform_or_ide other plan_or_license other
  • Has Layered instruction precedence (personal/repository/organization)
    GitHub documents personal, repository, and organization instruction scopes and an automatically supplied priority order: personal first, repository next, organization last. Repository scope additionally orders path-specific, repository-wide, and agent instructions. All three named scopes exist on GitHub.com, meeting both the hierarchy requirement and the stricter three-scope interpretation of the partial criterion.
    platform_or_ide plan_or_license other

Security & Governance

  • Has Enterprise SSO / access control
    Copilot Business enterprise accounts support SAML SSO for personal accounts or IdP-provisioned Enterprise Managed Users with SCIM and SSO. Enterprise teams govern licensing, and Copilot policies expose owner and custom-role permissions for AI controls and organizational settings. Together these establish SSO plus role/permission management, rather than merely basic team membership.
    plan_or_license integration_required plan_or_license
  • Has Data retention / training opt-out controls
    Current personal-policy documentation gives an explicit Disabled setting for Allow GitHub to use my data for AI model training on Free, Pro, Pro+, and Max. Business/Enterprise data is contractually protected from training without customer authorization, and that personal toggle is not displayed for these plans. This establishes the actionable training opt-out branch of the feature; it does not imply universal zero retention of prompts, responses, session logs, or telemetry.
    plan_or_license other
  • Uncertain On-premises / private cloud deployment
    No supported deployment of the Copilot service itself to customer infrastructure or a dedicated private-cloud instance was confirmed. The plans page explicitly excludes GitHub Enterprise Server. Self-hosted runners relocate the cloud agent's development environment, not the whole service, and isolated CLI BYOK is recorded under local model support rather than treated as proof of a private Copilot service. A complete negative finding is not justified: the product page and changelog index did not expose substantive body content through simplified fetching, and initial raw-HTML reads did not recover it. Consequently the broader private-deployment question remains uncertain rather than not_found.
    platform_or_ide other
  • Partial IP indemnity / public-code duplication filter
    Original Copilot documentation verifies an Allow/Block public-code matching setting and withholding matches or near matches. Current March 2026 organizational AI terms extend defense of third-party claims to outputs only when the customer's main agreement already provides that defense; they do not constitute an unconditional indemnity for every plan. Partial follows the assigned criterion for a documented filter with conditional, plan/contract-scoped legal protection. Historical product-specific terms and third-party study notes were not used to assert current indemnity.
    platform_or_ide plan_or_license plan_or_license other
  • Has Audit logging & usage metrics
    Administrators can monitor policy and access changes using audit logs, and cloud-agent session logs and audit events are available to administrators. Copilot usage metrics additionally expose enterprise, organization, repository, and user-level API reports and exports. These are organizational controls rather than personal history; documentation establishes Business as well as Enterprise governance, not an Enterprise-only logging restriction.
    plan_or_license platform_or_ide product_version other
  • Has Local / offline (BYO) model support
    GitHub documents supported customer-controlled local inference, including Ollama and other OpenAI-compatible endpoints, in Copilot CLI. Its offline mode prevents contact with GitHub servers when paired with a local or isolated provider. This is not limited to completions: the official release explicitly retains the agentic terminal experience. VS Code also supports local or self-hosted models for chat and utility tasks, although not every Copilot feature uses BYOK.
    model integration_required plan_or_license platform_or_ide release_stage
  • Has Secret detection & redaction
    A supported GitHub MCP integration provides automatic secret blocking in AI-generated responses and MCP write actions, including creation of files. This satisfies the output-blocking criterion within that integration; it is not evidence of universal prompt redaction before inference or interception of arbitrary local filesystem writes. Copilot cloud agent also automatically scans generated code and attempts remediation, but that post-generation validation alone would not establish pre-write blocking.
    integration_required plan_or_license other other release_stage
  • Has Agent network egress control / firewall
    Copilot cloud agent has a configurable outbound firewall with organization and repository allowlists for domains and URLs. Owners can enforce organization rules, control repository customization, and enable or disable the firewall. This is a network-specific execution control, not merely process isolation.
    platform_or_ide other plan_or_license
  • Has Data processing / residency region control
    GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency exposes the Restrict Copilot to data residency compliant models policy. Enabling it keeps inference processing, code, prompts, responses, and related logs/telemetry within the designated US or EU geography. This is an actionable regional restriction for processing as well as storage, not just a default location. The generic DPA's international-transfer permission does not override this more specific product control.
    plan_or_license region model product_version release_stage
  • Has Sub-processor / third-party data-sharing disclosure
    GitHub publishes a publicly accessible, itemized vendor-maintained subprocessor list under its official privacy documentation. It identifies processing functions and locations, including AI inference providers such as Anthropic and OpenAI. The list applies to GitHub services governed by the GitHub Data Protection Agreement; it is a service-wide disclosure rather than a claim that every listed provider processes every Copilot request.

  • Partial Data Processing Agreement (DPA) availability
    A concrete public GitHub Data Protection Agreement is available and incorporated into the executed customer agreement governing organizational online services. Copilot approval documentation expressly covers Business and Enterprise. General availability to personal consumer tiers is not established: the current Generative AI Services Terms exclude personal customers and Microsoft purchases. The tier-scoped partial criterion therefore applies, rather than inferring universal DPA access from a privacy policy.

  • Partial Encryption in transit & at rest
    Copilot's original network documentation explicitly describes a secure HTTPS connection, establishing in-transit encryption. No original retrieved page explicitly confirmed at-rest encryption of retained Copilot customer data. The DPA's generic encryption safeguards and encrypted passwords are insufficient to infer encryption of all stored customer code/data. Partial reflects the documented in-transit half only; inaccessible Trust Center content leaves the at-rest half unresolved, not absent.

Additional facts

Built-in tools

  • Named sub-agents:

    Copilot CLI documents seven built-in specialists: explore, task, general-purpose, code-review, research, rubber-duck, and security-review. Explore and the review specialists do not change files; task runs development commands and summarizes their output; rubber-duck offers a second opinion using a different model. These are CLI subagent roles, not a promise that every IDE exposes the same roster. Running a project's linters or formatters through task does not establish that Copilot bundles those tools.

    • “Copilot CLI includes the following built-in agents which the main agent can run as subagents to assist with common development tasks.”
    • “**task** — A command execution agent that runs development commands (tests, builds, linters, formatters, dependency installs) and reports results efficiently.”
    • “It runs on a different model from the one driving your session, so it brings a complementary perspective.”

Pricing & licensing

  • Pricing note:

    Current individual paid-plan allowances distinguish base credits from a flex allotment: Pro totals 1,500 monthly AI credits, Pro+ 7,000, and Max 20,000. The overview lists Business at 1,900 credits per user/month and Enterprise at 3,900. Free inline completions are limited to 2,000/month; Free and Student model access is auto-selection only. These are the checked current credit-based allowances, not historical premium-request quotas or a guarantee of unlimited agent work.

    • “| Plan | Price per month | Base credits | Flex allotment | Total monthly AI credits |”

    • “On Copilot Free and Copilot Student plans, access to models is available through auto model selection only.”
  • Plans & pricing:

    The official plans page checked on October 11, 2026 lists Pro at USD 10/month, Pro+ at USD 39/month, Max at USD 100/month, Business at USD 19 per granted seat/month, and Enterprise at USD 39 per granted seat/month. Free and verified Student plans are also listed. All plans include CLI and the Copilot app, but access, models, and usage allowances differ. Enterprise is designed for GitHub Enterprise Cloud, not Enterprise Server.

  • Plans and deployment:

    CLI 1.0.94-0 adds /model discovery of supported models from an already-running local Ollama instance. Adding a discovered model requires confirmation and does not install Ollama or download a model. Tool calling and streaming are required. Selecting a local model alone neither enables offline mode nor disables GitHub telemetry; COPILOT_OFFLINE=true is a separate explicit setting, and a remote provider can still receive code and prompts.

Security & data handling

  • Data usage:

    The October 6, 2026 changelog reports an attribution defect affecting SDK-based IDE agent sessions: most activity was omitted from usage reports and some was misattributed to CLI. The fix was available in VS Code 1.139.0 and later; other IDE fixes were still expected in later releases. Missing activity cannot be backfilled, historical CLI inflation cannot be corrected, and billing is unaffected. General telemetry minimum versions alone therefore do not guarantee complete agent reporting.

    • “Most of that activity was left out of reports, and some was counted as Copilot CLI activity.”
    • “| Visual Studio Code | 1.139.0 and later | Available now |”
    • “We can’t backfill missing data.”
    • “Billing isn’t affected.”
  • Data usage:

    Copilot automations are stored outside repository contents and are not versioned through Git or pull requests. An automation is private to its creator, even from repository administrators, while its resulting sessions, prompts, logs, and changes are visible to people with repository access. Runs consume Actions minutes and AI credits billed to the creator. Availability requires a private/internal repository, write access, an eligible paid plan, and enabled cloud-agent/automation policies.

    • “Automations are stored separately from your repository's contents. They are not committed to Git, so they are not versioned alongside your code or managed through pull requests.”
    • “An automation is **private to the user who created it**. Other people, including repository administrators, can't see your automations.”
    • “This usage is billed to the user who created the automation.”
  • Data usage:

    Current personal-policy documentation says GitHub may use Free, Pro, Pro+, and Max interactions for model training starting April 24, 2026. Users can disable the training setting. Business and Enterprise data is protected against model training without customer authorization and the personal toggle is not displayed for those plans. This distinction does not establish zero retention of prompts, outputs, logs, or telemetry.

    • “Starting on April 24, 2026, if you have a **Copilot Free**, **Copilot Pro**, **Copilot Pro+**, or **Copilot Max** plan, GitHub may use your interactions with GitHub features and services—including inputs, outputs, code snippets, and associated context—to train and improve AI models.”
    • “GitHub does not use Copilot Business or Copilot Enterprise customer data to train AI models.”
    • “Select the "Allow GitHub to use my data for AI model training" dropdown menu and click **Disabled**.”

Extensibility & MCP ecosystem

  • Extensibility via MCP:

    CLI supports local and remote MCP servers with GitHub's server built in. The app can reuse repository or CLI MCP configuration. Repository MCP settings apply to cloud agent and code review, where GitHub and Playwright servers are configured by default. Business/Enterprise MCP access is subject to an organization or enterprise policy disabled by default; that policy does not govern individual Free, Pro, Pro+, or Max access. The MCP Registry is a discovery catalog in public preview, not evidence that every listed server is vendor-supported.

    • “**Copilot CLI**: GitHub Copilot CLI supports both local and remote MCP servers. The GitHub MCP server is built in and available without additional configuration.”
    • “The configuration applies to both Copilot cloud agent and Copilot code review. The GitHub MCP server and Playwright MCP server are configured by default.”
    • “The policy is disabled by default.”
